e-7316.knowledge_point: Integrating a Rational Function Given Part Of the Partial Fraction Decomposition
e-7316.problem:
Given that 

$$
\dfrac{4x^2-6}{(x-3)(x^2+1)} = \dfrac{A}{x-3} + \dfrac{x+3}{x^2 + 1},
$$

where $A$ is a constant to be found, calculate $\displaystyle{\int \dfrac{4x^2-6}{(x-3)(x^2+1)}\,\textrm d x}.$
e-7316.worked_solution:
First, we find the constant $A.$ Multiplying both sides of the given equality by $(x-3)(x^2 + 1)$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}4{x}^{2}-6=A({x}^{2}+1)+{x}^{2}-9.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting $x=0$  into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}4(0)^{2}-6 & =A({0}^{2}+1)+{0}^{2}-9 \\ -6 & =A-9 \\ A & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

 

We now integrate this function term by term, adding the constant of integration at the very end.

$$
\eqalign{
\int \dfrac{4x^2 - 6}{(x-3)(x^2+1)} \, \textrm{d}x & = \int \left(\dfrac{3}{x-3} + \dfrac{x+3}{x^2 + 1}\right) \textrm{d}x \[5pt]

& = 3\int\dfrac{1}{x-3}\,\textrm{d}x + \int \dfrac{x}{x^2+1}\,\textrm d x + 3\int \dfrac{1}{x^2 + 1} \, \textrm{d}x
	}
$$

For the first integral, we get

$$
\int \dfrac{1}{x-3} \textrm{d}x = \ln|x-3|.
$$

For the second integral, we use the substitution $x^2 + 1 = u.$ Then, $2x\,\textrm{d}x=\textrm{d}u,$ and we get 

$$
\eqalign{
\int \dfrac{x}{x^2+1}\,\textrm{d}x & = \int \left(\dfrac{1}{u}\right) \dfrac{\textrm d u}{2} \[5pt]

&= \dfrac{1}{2}\ln \vert u\vert \[5pt]

&= \dfrac{1}{2}\ln \vert x^2 + 1\vert \[5pt]

& = \dfrac{1}{2}\ln \left(x^2+1\right).							
}
$$

Finally, for the third integral, we use the fact that $\displaystyle \int \dfrac{1}{x^2 + a^2} \, \textrm{d}x = \dfrac{1}{a}\arctan\left(\dfrac{x}{a}\right),$ which results in

$$
\int \dfrac{1}{x^2+1}\,\textrm{d}x = \arctan{x}.
$$

So, we get the following result:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{4{x}^{2}-6}{(x-3)({x}^{2}+1)}\,\text{d}x & =3\int \frac{1}{x-3}\,\text{d}x+\int \frac{x}{{x}^{2}+1}\,\text{d}x+3\int \frac{1}{{x}^{2}+1}\,\text{d}x \\  & =3\operatorname{ln}⁡|x-3|+\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+1)+3\operatorname{arctan}⁡x+C\end{aligned}
$$

e-4102.knowledge_point: Integrating a Rational Function With an Irreducible Binomial Quadratic Factor
e-4102.worked_solution:
The quadratic factor $x^2+4$ is irreducible, so we proceed with the following partial fraction decomposition:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{2x+3}{({x}^{2}+4)(x-1)} & =\frac{Ax+B}{({x}^{2}+4)}+\frac{C}{(x-1)}\end{aligned}
$$

To determine the coefficients $A,$ $B,$ and $C,$ we first multiply both sides of the above equation by $(x^2+4)(x-1),$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}2x+3 & =(Ax+B)(x-1)+C({x}^{2}+4)\,.\end{aligned}
$$

Solving for the unknown constants using the usual methods, we get $A=-1, B=1,$ and $C=1.$ Therefore,

$$
\dfrac{2x+3}{(x^2+4)(x-1)} = \dfrac{-x+1}{x^2+4} +\dfrac{1}{x-1}.
$$

Now we integrate this function term by term, adding the constant of integration at the very end.

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{2x+3}{({x}^{2}+4)(x-1)}\,\text{d}x & =\int (\frac{-x+1}{{x}^{2}+4}+\frac{1}{x-1})\text{d}x \\  & =-\int \frac{x}{{x}^{2}+4}\,\text{d}x+\int \frac{1}{{x}^{2}+4}\,\text{d}x+\int \frac{1}{x-1}\,\text{d}x\end{aligned}
$$

For the first integral, we use the substitution $u = x^2+4.$ Then $2x\,\textrm{d}x=\textrm{d}u,$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{x}{{x}^{2}+4}\,\text{d}x & =\int (\frac{1}{u})\frac{\text{d}u}{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡|u| \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡|{x}^{2}+4| \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+4).\end{aligned}
$$

For the second integral,  we use the fact that $\displaystyle \int \dfrac{1}{x^2+a^2} \, \textrm{d}x = \dfrac{1}{a}\arctan\left(\dfrac{x}{a}\right),$ which results in

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{1}{{x}^{2}+4}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{x}{2}).\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, for the third integral we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{1}{x-1}\text{d}x & =\operatorname{ln}⁡|x-1|.\end{aligned}
$$

So we get the following result:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{2x+3}{({x}^{2}+4)(x-1)}\,\text{d}x & =-\int \frac{x}{{x}^{2}+4}\,\text{d}x+\int \frac{1}{{x}^{2}+4}\,\text{d}x+\int \frac{1}{x-1}\,\text{d}x \\  & =-\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+4)+\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{x}{2})+\operatorname{ln}⁡|x-1|+K\end{aligned}
$$

e-510.knowledge_point: Integrating a Rational Function With an Irreducible Trinomial Quadratic Factor
e-510.worked_solution:
Notice that the quadratic factor in the denominator has a negative discriminant:

$$
\mathcal{D} = 1^2 - 4(1)(1) = -3 < 0
$$

So, we proceed with the following partial fraction decomposition:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{4{x}^{2}-x}{({x}^{2}+x+1)(x-2)} & =\frac{Ax+B}{{x}^{2}+x+1}+\frac{C}{x-2}\end{aligned}
$$

To determine the coefficients $A,$ $B,$ and $C,$ we first multiply both sides of the above equation by $(x^2+x+1)(x-2)$ and get

$$
\begin{aligned}4{x}^{2}-x & =(Ax+B)(x-2)+C({x}^{2}+x+1).\end{aligned}
$$

Solving for the unknown constants using the usual methods, we get  $A=2,$ $B=1,$ and $C=2.$ Therefore,

$$
\dfrac{4x^2-x}{(x^2+x+1)(x-2)} = \dfrac{2x+1}{x^2+x+1} + \dfrac{2}{x-2}.
$$

Now we integrate this function term by term, adding the constant of integration only at the very end.

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{4{x}^{2}-x}{({x}^{2}+x+1)(x-2)}\,\text{d}x & =\int (\frac{2x+1}{{x}^{2}+x+1}+\frac{2}{x-2})\text{d}x \\  & =\int \frac{2x+1}{{x}^{2}+x+1}\,\text{d}x+2\int \frac{1}{x-2}\,\text{d}x\end{aligned}
$$

For the first integral, we use the substitution $u = x^2+x+1.$ Then $(2x+1) \, \textrm{d}x=\textrm{d}u,$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{2x+1}{{x}^{2}+x+1}\,\text{d}x & =\int (\frac{1}{u})\text{d}u \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡|u| \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡|{x}^{2}+x+1| \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+x+1).\end{aligned}
$$

For the second integral we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{1}{x-2}\,\text{d}x & =\operatorname{ln}⁡|x-2|.\end{aligned}
$$

So we get the following result:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{4{x}^{2}-x}{({x}^{2}+x+1)(x-2)}\,\text{d}x & =\int \frac{2x+1}{{x}^{2}+x+1}\,\text{d}x+2\int \frac{1}{x-2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+x+1)+2\operatorname{ln}⁡|x-2|+K\end{aligned}
$$

before.html:
Question 1
?

Given that x2−5x−27(x+1)(x2+20)=2x+Bx2+20−1x+1, where B is a constant to be found, calculate ∫x2−5x−27(x+1)(x2+20)dx.

a
 ln⁡(x2+20)+5arctan⁡(5x10)+2ln⁡|x+1|+C
b
 ln⁡(x2+20)−75arctan⁡(x5)−ln⁡|x+1|+C
c
 ln⁡(x2+20)−510arctan⁡(5x10)+C
d
 ln⁡(x2+20)−7510arctan⁡(5x10)−ln⁡|x+1|+C
e
 ln⁡(x2+20)−55arctan⁡(5x5)+C
Submit

decision.explanation: Clearing denominators gives x²−5x−27=(2x+B)(x+1)−(x²+20)=x²+(B+2)x+B−20, so B=−7. Integrating term by term gives ln(x²+20)−(7/√20)arctan(x/√20)−ln|x+1|+C. Since 1/√20=√5/10, this is option d.

after.name: Question 1
after.problem:
Given that 

$$
\frac{{x}^{2}-5x-27}{(x+1)({x}^{2}+20)}=\frac{2x+B}{{x}^{2}+20}-\frac{1}{x+1},
$$

where $B$ is a constant to be found, calculate $\int \frac{{x}^{2}-5x-27}{(x+1)({x}^{2}+20)}\,\text{d}x.$
after.worked_solution:
First, we find the constant $B.$ Multiplying both sides of the given equality by $(x+1)({x}^{2}+20)$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}-5x-27 & =(2x+B)(x+1)-({x}^{2}+20).\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting $x=0$  into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{0}^{2}-5(0)-27 & =(2(0)+B)(0+1)-({0}^{2}+20) \\ -27 & =B-20 \\ B & =-7.\end{aligned}
$$

 

We now integrate this function term by term, adding the constant of integration at the very end.

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{{x}^{2}-5x-27}{(x+1)({x}^{2}+20)}\,\text{d}x & =\int (\frac{2x-7}{{x}^{2}+20}-\frac{1}{x+1})\text{d}x \\  & =\int \frac{2x}{{x}^{2}+20}\,\text{d}x-7\int \frac{1}{{x}^{2}+20}\,\text{d}x-\int \frac{1}{x+1}\text{d}x\end{aligned}
$$

For the first integral, we use the substitution ${x}^{2}+20=u.$ Then, $2x\,\text{d}x=\text{d}u,$ and we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{2x}{{x}^{2}+20}\,\text{d}x & =\int \frac{1}{u}\,\text{d}u \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡|u| \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+20).\end{aligned}
$$

For the second integral, we use the fact that $\int \frac{1}{{x}^{2}+{a}^{2}}\,\text{d}x=\frac{1}{a}\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{x}{a}),$ which results in

$$
\begin{aligned}7\int \frac{1}{{x}^{2}+20}\,\text{d}x & =7\int \frac{1}{{x}^{2}+(2\sqrt{5})^{2}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =7\cdot \frac{1}{2\sqrt{5}}\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{x}{2\sqrt{5}}) \\  & =\frac{7\sqrt{5}}{10}\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{\sqrt{5}x}{10}).\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, for the third integral, we get

$$
\int \frac{1}{x+1}\text{d}x=\operatorname{ln}⁡|x+1|.
$$

So, we get the following result:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{{x}^{2}-5x-27}{(x+1)({x}^{2}+20)}\,\text{d}x & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+20)-\frac{7\sqrt{5}}{10}\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{\sqrt{5}x}{10})-\operatorname{ln}⁡|x+1|+C\end{aligned}
$$

a

b

c

d

EXPLANATION

First, we find the constant B. Multiplying both sides of the given equality by (x+1)(x2+20) gives

x2−5x−27=(2x+B)(x+1)−(x2+20).

Substituting x=0 into the above gives 02−5(0)−27=(2(0)+B)(0+1)−(02+20)−27=B−20B=−7.

We now integrate this function term by term, adding the constant of integration at the very end. ∫x2−5x−27(x+1)(x2+20)dx=∫(2x−7x2+20−1x+1)dx=∫2xx2+20dx−7∫1x2+20dx−∫1x+1dx

For the first integral, we use the substitution x2+20=u. Then, 2xdx=du, and we get ∫2xx2+20dx=∫1udu=ln⁡|u|=ln⁡(x2+20).

For the second integral, we use the fact that ∫1x2+a2dx=1aarctan⁡(xa), which results in 7∫1x2+20dx=7∫1x2+(25)2dx=7⋅125arctan⁡(x25)=7510arctan⁡(5x10).

Finally, for the third integral, we get ∫1x+1dx=ln⁡|x+1|.

So, we get the following result: ∫x2−5x−27(x+1)(x2+20)dx=ln⁡(x2+20)−7510arctan⁡(5x10)−ln⁡|x+1|+C

content.knowledge_point: Integrating a Rational Function Given Part Of the Partial Fraction Decomposition
content.problem:
Given that 

$$
\frac{{x}^{2}-5x-27}{(x+1)({x}^{2}+20)}=\frac{2x+B}{{x}^{2}+20}-\frac{1}{x+1},
$$

where $B$ is a constant to be found, calculate $\int \frac{{x}^{2}-5x-27}{(x+1)({x}^{2}+20)}\,\text{d}x.$
content.worked_solution:
First, we find the constant $B.$ Multiplying both sides of the given equality by $(x+1)({x}^{2}+20)$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}-5x-27 & =(2x+B)(x+1)-({x}^{2}+20).\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting $x=0$  into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{0}^{2}-5(0)-27 & =(2(0)+B)(0+1)-({0}^{2}+20) \\ -27 & =B-20 \\ B & =-7.\end{aligned}
$$

 

We now integrate this function term by term, adding the constant of integration at the very end.

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{{x}^{2}-5x-27}{(x+1)({x}^{2}+20)}\,\text{d}x & =\int (\frac{2x-7}{{x}^{2}+20}-\frac{1}{x+1})\text{d}x \\  & =\int \frac{2x}{{x}^{2}+20}\,\text{d}x-7\int \frac{1}{{x}^{2}+20}\,\text{d}x-\int \frac{1}{x+1}\text{d}x\end{aligned}
$$

For the first integral, we use the substitution ${x}^{2}+20=u.$ Then, $2x\,\text{d}x=\text{d}u,$ and we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{2x}{{x}^{2}+20}\,\text{d}x & =\int \frac{1}{u}\,\text{d}u \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡|u| \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+20).\end{aligned}
$$

For the second integral, we use the fact that $\int \frac{1}{{x}^{2}+{a}^{2}}\,\text{d}x=\frac{1}{a}\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{x}{a}),$ which results in

$$
\begin{aligned}7\int \frac{1}{{x}^{2}+20}\,\text{d}x & =7\int \frac{1}{{x}^{2}+(2\sqrt{5})^{2}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =7\cdot \frac{1}{2\sqrt{5}}\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{x}{2\sqrt{5}}) \\  & =\frac{7\sqrt{5}}{10}\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{\sqrt{5}x}{10}).\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, for the third integral, we get

$$
\int \frac{1}{x+1}\text{d}x=\operatorname{ln}⁡|x+1|.
$$

So, we get the following result:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{{x}^{2}-5x-27}{(x+1)({x}^{2}+20)}\,\text{d}x & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+20)-\frac{7\sqrt{5}}{10}\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{\sqrt{5}x}{10})-\operatorname{ln}⁡|x+1|+C\end{aligned}
$$

before.html:
Question 2
?

Given that 4x2+20(x+2)(x2+8)=x−2x2+8+Dx+2, where D is a constant to be found, calculate ∫4x2+20(x+2)(x2+8)dx.

a
 −12ln⁡(x2+8)+22arctan⁡(2x4)+12ln⁡|x+2|+C
b
 12ln⁡(x2+8)−22arctan⁡(2x4)+3ln⁡|x+2|+C
c
 12ln⁡(x2+8)−22arctan⁡(2x4)+C
d
 ln⁡(x2+8)+22arctan⁡(2x4)−ln⁡|x+2|+C
e
 ln⁡(x2+8)−2arctan⁡(2x4)+2ln⁡|x+2|+C
Submit

decision.explanation: Clearing denominators gives 4x²+20=(x−2)(x+2)+D(x²+8)=(1+D)x²+8D−4, so D=3. Integrating (x−2)/(x²+8)+3/(x+2) gives ½ln(x²+8)−(√2/2)arctan(√2x/4)+3ln|x+2|+C, matching option b.

after.name: Question 2
after.problem:
Given that 

$$
\frac{4{x}^{2}+20}{(x+2)({x}^{2}+8)}=\frac{x-2}{{x}^{2}+8}+\frac{D}{x+2},
$$

where $D$ is a constant to be found, calculate $\int \frac{4{x}^{2}+20}{(x+2)({x}^{2}+8)}\,\text{d}x.$
after.worked_solution:
First, we find the constant $D.$ Multiplying both sides of the given equality by $(x+2)({x}^{2}+8)$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}4{x}^{2}+20 & =(x-2)(x+2)+D({x}^{2}+8).\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting $x=0$  into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}4(0)^{2}+20 & =(0-2)(0+2)+D({0}^{2}+8) \\ 20 & =-4+8D \\ 24 & =8D \\ D & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

 

We now integrate this function term by term, adding the constant of integration at the very end.

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{4{x}^{2}+20}{(x+2)({x}^{2}+8)}\,\text{d}x & =\int (\frac{x-2}{{x}^{2}+8}+\frac{3}{x+2})\text{d}x \\  & =\int \frac{x}{{x}^{2}+8}\,\text{d}x-2\int \frac{1}{{x}^{2}+8}\,\text{d}x+3\int \frac{1}{x+2}\,\text{d}x\end{aligned}
$$

For the first integral, we use the substitution ${x}^{2}+8=u.$ Then, $x\,\text{d}x=\frac{1}{2}\,\text{d}u,$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{x}{{x}^{2}+8}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{1}{2}\int \frac{1}{u}\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡|u| \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+8).\end{aligned}
$$

For the second integral, we use the fact that $\int \frac{1}{{x}^{2}+{a}^{2}}\,\text{d}x=\frac{1}{a}\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{x}{a}),$ which results in

$$
\begin{aligned}2\int \frac{1}{{x}^{2}+8}\,\text{d}x & =2\int \frac{1}{{x}^{2}+(2\sqrt{2})^{2}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =2\cdot \frac{1}{2\sqrt{2}}\cdot \operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{x}{2\sqrt{2}}) \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\cdot \operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{\sqrt{2}x}{4}).\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, for the third integral, we get

$$
3\int \frac{1}{x+2}\text{d}x=3\operatorname{ln}⁡|x+2|.
$$

So, we get the following result:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{4{x}^{2}+20}{(x+2)({x}^{2}+8)}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+8)-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{\sqrt{2}x}{4})+3\operatorname{ln}⁡|x+2|+C\end{aligned}
$$

Given that 4x2+20(x+2)(x2+8)=x−2x2+8+Dx+2, where D is a constant to be found, calculate ∫4x2+20(x+2)(x2+8)dx.

a
 −12ln⁡(x2+8)+22arctan⁡(2x4)+12ln⁡|x+2|+C
b
 12ln⁡(x2+8)−22arctan⁡(2x4)+3ln⁡|x+2|+C
c
 12ln⁡(x2+8)−22arctan⁡(2x4)+C
d
 ln⁡(x2+8)+22arctan⁡(2x4)−ln⁡|x+2|+C
e
 ln⁡(x2+8)−2arctan⁡(2x4)+2ln⁡|x+2|+C
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, we find the constant D. Multiplying both sides of the given equality by (x+2)(x2+8) gives 4x2+20=(x−2)(x+2)+D(x2+8).

Substituting x=0 into the above gives 4(0)2+20=(0−2)(0+2)+D(02+8)20=−4+8D24=8DD=3.

We now integrate this function term by term, adding the constant of integration at the very end. ∫4x2+20(x+2)(x2+8)dx=∫(x−2x2+8+3x+2)dx=∫xx2+8dx−2∫1x2+8dx+3∫1x+2dx

For the first integral, we use the substitution x2+8=u. Then, xdx=12du, and we get
∫xx2+8dx=12∫1udu=12ln⁡|u|=12ln⁡(x2+8).

For the second integral, we use the fact that ∫1x2+a2dx=1aarctan⁡(xa), which results in 2∫1x2+8dx=2∫1x2+(22)2dx=2⋅122⋅arctan⁡(x22)=22⋅arctan⁡(2x4).

Finally, for the third integral, we get 3∫1x+2dx=3ln⁡|x+2|.

So, we get the following result: ∫4x2+20(x+2)(x2+8)dx=12ln⁡(x2+8)−22arctan⁡(2x4)+3ln⁡|x+2|+C

content.knowledge_point: Integrating a Rational Function Given Part Of the Partial Fraction Decomposition
content.problem:
Given that 

$$
\frac{4{x}^{2}+20}{(x+2)({x}^{2}+8)}=\frac{x-2}{{x}^{2}+8}+\frac{D}{x+2},
$$

where $D$ is a constant to be found, calculate $\int \frac{4{x}^{2}+20}{(x+2)({x}^{2}+8)}\,\text{d}x.$
content.worked_solution:
First, we find the constant $D.$ Multiplying both sides of the given equality by $(x+2)({x}^{2}+8)$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}4{x}^{2}+20 & =(x-2)(x+2)+D({x}^{2}+8).\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting $x=0$  into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}4(0)^{2}+20 & =(0-2)(0+2)+D({0}^{2}+8) \\ 20 & =-4+8D \\ 24 & =8D \\ D & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

 

We now integrate this function term by term, adding the constant of integration at the very end.

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{4{x}^{2}+20}{(x+2)({x}^{2}+8)}\,\text{d}x & =\int (\frac{x-2}{{x}^{2}+8}+\frac{3}{x+2})\text{d}x \\  & =\int \frac{x}{{x}^{2}+8}\,\text{d}x-2\int \frac{1}{{x}^{2}+8}\,\text{d}x+3\int \frac{1}{x+2}\,\text{d}x\end{aligned}
$$

For the first integral, we use the substitution ${x}^{2}+8=u.$ Then, $x\,\text{d}x=\frac{1}{2}\,\text{d}u,$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{x}{{x}^{2}+8}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{1}{2}\int \frac{1}{u}\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡|u| \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+8).\end{aligned}
$$

For the second integral, we use the fact that $\int \frac{1}{{x}^{2}+{a}^{2}}\,\text{d}x=\frac{1}{a}\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{x}{a}),$ which results in

$$
\begin{aligned}2\int \frac{1}{{x}^{2}+8}\,\text{d}x & =2\int \frac{1}{{x}^{2}+(2\sqrt{2})^{2}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =2\cdot \frac{1}{2\sqrt{2}}\cdot \operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{x}{2\sqrt{2}}) \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\cdot \operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{\sqrt{2}x}{4}).\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, for the third integral, we get

$$
3\int \frac{1}{x+2}\text{d}x=3\operatorname{ln}⁡|x+2|.
$$

So, we get the following result:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{4{x}^{2}+20}{(x+2)({x}^{2}+8)}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+8)-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{\sqrt{2}x}{4})+3\operatorname{ln}⁡|x+2|+C\end{aligned}
$$

Question 3
?

Given that x2+x+3(x2+4)(x−1)=Ax+1x2+4+1x−1, where A is a constant to be found, calculate ∫x2+x+3(x2+4)(x−1)dx.

a
ln⁡|x2+4|+12arctan⁡(x2)+C
b
12ln⁡|x2+4|+14arctan⁡(x4)+ln⁡|x−1|+C
c
12ln⁡|x2+4|+ln⁡|x−1|+C
d
ln⁡|x2+4|+12arctan⁡(x2)+ln⁡|x−1|+C
e
12arctan⁡(x2)+ln⁡|x−1|+C
Submit

decision.explanation: Clearing denominators gives x²+x+3=(Ax+1)(x−1)+(x²+4)=(A+1)x²+(1−A)x+3, so A=0. Thus the integral is ∫1/(x²+4) dx+∫1/(x−1) dx=½arctan(x/2)+ln|x−1|+C, matching option e.

after.name: Question 3
after.problem:
Given that 

$$
\frac{{x}^{2}+x+3}{({x}^{2}+4)(x-1)}=\frac{Ax+1}{{x}^{2}+4}+\frac{1}{x-1},
$$

where $A$ is a constant to be found, calculate $\int \frac{{x}^{2}+x+3}{({x}^{2}+4)(x-1)}\,\text{d}x.$
after.worked_solution:
First, we find the constant $A.$ Multiplying both sides of the given equality by $({x}^{2}+4)(x-1)$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}+x+3 & =(Ax+1)(x-1)+{x}^{2}+4.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting $x=2$  into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{2}^{2}+2+3 & =(A(2)+1)(2-1)+{2}^{2}+4 \\ 9 & =2A+1+8 \\ 9 & =2A+9 \\ A & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

 

We now integrate this function term by term, adding the constant of integration at the very end.

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{{x}^{2}+x+3}{({x}^{2}+4)(x-1)}\,\text{d}x & =\int (\frac{0x+1}{{x}^{2}+4}+\frac{1}{x-1})\text{d}x \\  & =\int \frac{1}{{x}^{2}+4}\,\text{d}x+\int \frac{1}{x-1}\,\text{d}x\end{aligned}
$$

For the first integral, we use the fact that $\int \frac{1}{{x}^{2}+{a}^{2}}\,\text{d}x=\frac{1}{a}\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{x}{a}),$ which results in

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{1}{{x}^{2}+4}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{x}{2}).\end{aligned}
$$

For the second integral, we get

$$
\int \frac{1}{x-1}\,\text{d}x=\operatorname{ln}⁡|x-1|.
$$

So, we get the following result:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{{x}^{2}+x+3}{({x}^{2}+4)(x-1)}\,\text{d}x & =\int \frac{1}{{x}^{2}+4}\,\text{d}x+\int \frac{1}{x-1}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{x}{2})+\operatorname{ln}⁡|x-1|+C\end{aligned}
$$

Given that x2+x+3(x2+4)(x−1)=Ax+1x2+4+1x−1, where A is a constant to be found, calculate ∫x2+x+3(x2+4)(x−1)dx.

a
ln⁡|x2+4|+12arctan⁡(x2)+C
b
12ln⁡|x2+4|+14arctan⁡(x4)+ln⁡|x−1|+C
c
12ln⁡|x2+4|+ln⁡|x−1|+C
d
ln⁡|x2+4|+12arctan⁡(x2)+ln⁡|x−1|+C
e
12arctan⁡(x2)+ln⁡|x−1|+C
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

First, we find the constant A. Multiplying both sides of the given equality by (x2+4)(x−1) gives

x2+x+3=(Ax+1)(x−1)+x2+4.

Substituting x=2 into the above gives

22+2+3=(A(2)+1)(2−1)+22+49=2A+1+89=2A+9A=0.

We now integrate this function term by term, adding the constant of integration at the very end. ∫x2+x+3(x2+4)(x−1)dx=∫(0x+1x2+4+1x−1)dx=∫1x2+4dx+∫1x−1dx

For the first integral, we use the fact that ∫1x2+a2dx=1aarctan⁡(xa), which results in ∫1x2+4dx=12arctan⁡(x2).

For the second integral, we get ∫1x−1dx=ln⁡|x−1|.

So, we get the following result: ∫x2+x+3(x2+4)(x−1)dx=∫1x2+4dx+∫1x−1dx=12arctan⁡(x2)+ln⁡|x−1|+C

content.knowledge_point: Integrating a Rational Function Given Part Of the Partial Fraction Decomposition
content.problem:
Given that 

$$
\frac{{x}^{2}+x+3}{({x}^{2}+4)(x-1)}=\frac{Ax+1}{{x}^{2}+4}+\frac{1}{x-1},
$$

where $A$ is a constant to be found, calculate $\int \frac{{x}^{2}+x+3}{({x}^{2}+4)(x-1)}\,\text{d}x.$
content.worked_solution:
First, we find the constant $A.$ Multiplying both sides of the given equality by $({x}^{2}+4)(x-1)$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}+x+3 & =(Ax+1)(x-1)+{x}^{2}+4.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting $x=2$  into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{2}^{2}+2+3 & =(A(2)+1)(2-1)+{2}^{2}+4 \\ 9 & =2A+1+8 \\ 9 & =2A+9 \\ A & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

 

We now integrate this function term by term, adding the constant of integration at the very end.

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{{x}^{2}+x+3}{({x}^{2}+4)(x-1)}\,\text{d}x & =\int (\frac{0x+1}{{x}^{2}+4}+\frac{1}{x-1})\text{d}x \\  & =\int \frac{1}{{x}^{2}+4}\,\text{d}x+\int \frac{1}{x-1}\,\text{d}x\end{aligned}
$$

For the first integral, we use the fact that $\int \frac{1}{{x}^{2}+{a}^{2}}\,\text{d}x=\frac{1}{a}\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{x}{a}),$ which results in

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{1}{{x}^{2}+4}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{x}{2}).\end{aligned}
$$

For the second integral, we get

$$
\int \frac{1}{x-1}\,\text{d}x=\operatorname{ln}⁡|x-1|.
$$

So, we get the following result:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{{x}^{2}+x+3}{({x}^{2}+4)(x-1)}\,\text{d}x & =\int \frac{1}{{x}^{2}+4}\,\text{d}x+\int \frac{1}{x-1}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{x}{2})+\operatorname{ln}⁡|x-1|+C\end{aligned}
$$

before.html:
Question 4
?

Given that 3x2+4x+3(x2+3)(x+2)=2xx2+3+Dx+2, where D is a constant to be found, calculate ∫3x2+4x+3(x2+3)(x+2)dx.

a
33arctan⁡(33x)+ln⁡|x+2|+C
b
2ln⁡(x2+3)+33arctan⁡(33x)+C
c
ln⁡(x2+3)+ln⁡|x+2|+C
d
ln⁡(x2+3)−2ln⁡|x+2|+C
e
ln⁡(x2+3)+33arctan⁡(33x)+ln⁡|x+2|+C
Submit

decision.explanation: Clearing denominators gives 3x²+4x+3=2x(x+2)+D(x²+3), so D=1. Integrating 2x/(x²+3)+1/(x+2) gives ln(x²+3)+ln|x+2|+C, matching option c.

after.name: Question 4
after.problem:
Given that 

$$
\frac{3{x}^{2}+4x+3}{({x}^{2}+3)(x+2)}=\frac{2x}{{x}^{2}+3}+\frac{D}{x+2},
$$

where $D$ is a constant to be found, calculate $\int \frac{3{x}^{2}+4x+3}{({x}^{2}+3)(x+2)}\,\text{d}x.$
after.worked_solution:
First, we find the constant $D.$ Multiplying both sides of the given equality by $({x}^{2}+3)(x+2)$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}3{x}^{2}+4x+3 & =2x(x+2)+D({x}^{2}+3).\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting $x=-2$  into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}3(-2)^{2}+4(-2)+3 & =2(-2)(-2+2)+D((-2)^{2}+3) \\ 7 & =7D \\ D & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

 

We now integrate this function term by term, adding the constant of integration at the very end.

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{3{x}^{2}+4x+3}{({x}^{2}+3)(x+2)}\,\text{d}x & =\int (\frac{2x}{{x}^{2}+3}+\frac{1}{x+2})\text{d}x \\  & =\int \frac{2x}{{x}^{2}+3}\,\text{d}x+\int \frac{1}{x+2}\,\text{d}x\end{aligned}
$$

For the first integral, we use the substitution ${x}^{2}+3=u.$ Then, $2x\,\text{d}x=\text{d}u,$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{2x}{{x}^{2}+3}\,\text{d}x & =\int \frac{1}{u}\,\text{d}u \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡|u| \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡|{x}^{2}+3| \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+3).\end{aligned}
$$

For the second integral, we get

$$
\int \frac{1}{x+2}\,\text{d}x=\operatorname{ln}⁡|x+2|.
$$

So, we get the following result:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{3{x}^{2}+4x+3}{({x}^{2}+3)(x+2)}\,\text{d}x & =\int \frac{2x}{{x}^{2}+3}\,\text{d}x+\int \frac{1}{x+2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+3)+\operatorname{ln}⁡|x+2|+C\end{aligned}
$$

Question 4
?

Given that 3x2+4x+3(x2+3)(x+2)=2xx2+3+Dx+2, where D is a constant to be found, calculate ∫3x2+4x+3(x2+3)(x+2)dx.

a
33arctan⁡(33x)+ln⁡|x+2|+C
b
2ln⁡(x2+3)+33arctan⁡(33x)+C
c
ln⁡(x2+3)+ln⁡|x+2|+C
d
ln⁡(x2+3)−2ln⁡|x+2|+C
e
ln⁡(x2+3)+33arctan⁡(33x)+ln⁡|x+2|+C
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, we find the constant D. Multiplying both sides of the given equality by (x2+3)(x+2) gives 3x2+4x+3=2x(x+2)+D(x2+3).

Substituting x=−2 into the above gives 3(−2)2+4(−2)+3=2(−2)(−2+2)+D((−2)2+3)7=7DD=1.

We now integrate this function term by term, adding the constant of integration at the very end. ∫3x2+4x+3(x2+3)(x+2)dx=∫(2xx2+3+1x+2)dx=∫2xx2+3dx+∫1x+2dx

For the first integral, we use the substitution x2+3=u. Then, 2xdx=du, and we get
∫2xx2+3dx=∫1udu=ln⁡|u|=ln⁡|x2+3|=ln⁡(x2+3).

For the second integral, we get ∫1x+2dx=ln⁡|x+2|.

So, we get the following result: ∫3x2+4x+3(x2+3)(x+2)dx=∫2xx2+3dx+∫1x+2dx=ln⁡(x2+3)+ln⁡|x+2|+C

content.knowledge_point: Integrating a Rational Function Given Part Of the Partial Fraction Decomposition
content.problem:
Given that 

$$
\frac{3{x}^{2}+4x+3}{({x}^{2}+3)(x+2)}=\frac{2x}{{x}^{2}+3}+\frac{D}{x+2},
$$

where $D$ is a constant to be found, calculate $\int \frac{3{x}^{2}+4x+3}{({x}^{2}+3)(x+2)}\,\text{d}x.$
content.worked_solution:
First, we find the constant $D.$ Multiplying both sides of the given equality by $({x}^{2}+3)(x+2)$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}3{x}^{2}+4x+3 & =2x(x+2)+D({x}^{2}+3).\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting $x=-2$  into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}3(-2)^{2}+4(-2)+3 & =2(-2)(-2+2)+D((-2)^{2}+3) \\ 7 & =7D \\ D & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

 

We now integrate this function term by term, adding the constant of integration at the very end.

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{3{x}^{2}+4x+3}{({x}^{2}+3)(x+2)}\,\text{d}x & =\int (\frac{2x}{{x}^{2}+3}+\frac{1}{x+2})\text{d}x \\  & =\int \frac{2x}{{x}^{2}+3}\,\text{d}x+\int \frac{1}{x+2}\,\text{d}x\end{aligned}
$$

For the first integral, we use the substitution ${x}^{2}+3=u.$ Then, $2x\,\text{d}x=\text{d}u,$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{2x}{{x}^{2}+3}\,\text{d}x & =\int \frac{1}{u}\,\text{d}u \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡|u| \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡|{x}^{2}+3| \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+3).\end{aligned}
$$

For the second integral, we get

$$
\int \frac{1}{x+2}\,\text{d}x=\operatorname{ln}⁡|x+2|.
$$

So, we get the following result:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{3{x}^{2}+4x+3}{({x}^{2}+3)(x+2)}\,\text{d}x & =\int \frac{2x}{{x}^{2}+3}\,\text{d}x+\int \frac{1}{x+2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+3)+\operatorname{ln}⁡|x+2|+C\end{aligned}
$$

Question 5
?

Given that x2+5x−2(x+1)(x2+5)=2x+Bx2+5−1x+1, where B is a constant to be found, calculate ∫x2+5x−2(x+1)(x2+5)dx.

a
 −2ln⁡(x2+5)−455arctan⁡(5x5)+C
b
 355arctan⁡(5x5)−2ln⁡|x+1|+C
c
 ln⁡(x2+5)−25arctan⁡(x5)−ln⁡|x+1|+C
d
 −ln⁡(x2+5)+5arctan⁡(5x5)+2ln⁡|x+1|+C
e
 ln⁡(x2+5)+355arctan⁡(5x5)−ln⁡|x+1|+C
Submit

decision.explanation: Clearing denominators gives x²+5x−2=(2x+B)(x+1)−(x²+5)=x²+(B+2)x+B−5, so B=3. Integrating term by term yields ln(x²+5)+(3/√5)arctan(x/√5)−ln|x+1|+C, which is option e.

after.name: Question 5
after.problem:
Given that 

$$
\frac{{x}^{2}+5x-2}{(x+1)({x}^{2}+5)}=\frac{2x+B}{{x}^{2}+5}-\frac{1}{x+1},
$$

where $B$ is a constant to be found, calculate $\int \frac{{x}^{2}+5x-2}{(x+1)({x}^{2}+5)}\,\text{d}x.$
after.worked_solution:
First, we find the constant $B.$ Multiplying both sides of the given equality by $(x+1)({x}^{2}+5)$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}+5x-2 & =(2x+B)(x+1)-({x}^{2}+5).\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting $x=0$  into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{0}^{2}+5(0)-2 & =(2(0)+B)(0+1)-({0}^{2}+5) \\ -2 & =B-5 \\ B & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

 

We now integrate this function term by term, adding the constant of integration at the very end.

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{{x}^{2}+5x-2}{(x+1)({x}^{2}+5)}\,\text{d}x & =\int (\frac{2x+3}{{x}^{2}+5}-\frac{1}{x+1})\text{d}x \\  & =\int \frac{2x}{{x}^{2}+5}\,\text{d}x+\int \frac{3}{{x}^{2}+5}\,\text{d}x-\int \frac{1}{x+1}\,\text{d}x\end{aligned}
$$

For the first integral, we use the substitution ${x}^{2}+5=u.$ Then, $2x\,\text{d}x=\text{d}u,$ and we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{2x}{{x}^{2}+5}\,\text{d}x & =\int \frac{1}{u}\,\text{d}u \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡|u| \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+5).\end{aligned}
$$

For the second integral, we use the fact that $\int \frac{1}{{x}^{2}+{a}^{2}}\,\text{d}x=\frac{1}{a}\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{x}{a}),$ which results in

$$
\begin{aligned}3\int \frac{1}{{x}^{2}+5}\,\text{d}x & =3\int \frac{1}{{x}^{2}+(\sqrt{5})^{2}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{3}{\sqrt{5}}\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{x}{\sqrt{5}}) \\  & =\frac{3\sqrt{5}}{5}\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{\sqrt{5}x}{5}).\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, for the third integral, we get

$$
\int \frac{1}{x+1}\text{d}x=\operatorname{ln}⁡|x+1|.
$$

So, we get the following result:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{{x}^{2}+5x-2}{(x+1)({x}^{2}+5)}\,\text{d}x & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+5)+\frac{3\sqrt{5}}{5}\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{\sqrt{5}x}{5})-\operatorname{ln}⁡|x+1|+C\end{aligned}
$$

Question 5
?

Given that x2+5x−2(x+1)(x2+5)=2x+Bx2+5−1x+1, where B is a constant to be found, calculate ∫x2+5x−2(x+1)(x2+5)dx.

a
 −2ln⁡(x2+5)−455arctan⁡(5x5)+C
b
 355arctan⁡(5x5)−2ln⁡|x+1|+C
c
 ln⁡(x2+5)−25arctan⁡(x5)−ln⁡|x+1|+C
d
 −ln⁡(x2+5)+5arctan⁡(5x5)+2ln⁡|x+1|+C
e
 ln⁡(x2+5)+355arctan⁡(5x5)−ln⁡|x+1|+C
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, we find the constant B. Multiplying both sides of the given equality by (x+1)(x2+5) gives

x2+5x−2=(2x+B)(x+1)−(x2+5).

Substituting x=0 into the above gives

02+5(0)−2=(2(0)+B)(0+1)−(02+5)−2=B−5B=3.

We now integrate this function term by term, adding the constant of integration at the very end. ∫x2+5x−2(x+1)(x2+5)dx=∫(2x+3x2+5−1x+1)dx=∫2xx2+5dx+∫3x2+5dx−∫1x+1dx

For the first integral, we use the substitution x2+5=u. Then, 2xdx=du, and we get ∫2xx2+5dx=∫1udu=ln⁡|u|=ln⁡(x2+5).

For the second integral, we use the fact that ∫1x2+a2dx=1aarctan⁡(xa), which results in 3∫1x2+5dx=3∫1x2+(5)2dx=35arctan⁡(x5)=355arctan⁡(5x5).

Finally, for the third integral, we get ∫1x+1dx=ln⁡|x+1|.

So, we get the following result: ∫x2+5x−2(x+1)(x2+5)dx=ln⁡(x2+5)+355arctan⁡(5x5)−ln⁡|x+1|+C

content.knowledge_point: Integrating a Rational Function Given Part Of the Partial Fraction Decomposition
content.problem:
Given that 

$$
\frac{{x}^{2}+5x-2}{(x+1)({x}^{2}+5)}=\frac{2x+B}{{x}^{2}+5}-\frac{1}{x+1},
$$

where $B$ is a constant to be found, calculate $\int \frac{{x}^{2}+5x-2}{(x+1)({x}^{2}+5)}\,\text{d}x.$
content.worked_solution:
First, we find the constant $B.$ Multiplying both sides of the given equality by $(x+1)({x}^{2}+5)$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}+5x-2 & =(2x+B)(x+1)-({x}^{2}+5).\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting $x=0$  into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{0}^{2}+5(0)-2 & =(2(0)+B)(0+1)-({0}^{2}+5) \\ -2 & =B-5 \\ B & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

 

We now integrate this function term by term, adding the constant of integration at the very end.

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{{x}^{2}+5x-2}{(x+1)({x}^{2}+5)}\,\text{d}x & =\int (\frac{2x+3}{{x}^{2}+5}-\frac{1}{x+1})\text{d}x \\  & =\int \frac{2x}{{x}^{2}+5}\,\text{d}x+\int \frac{3}{{x}^{2}+5}\,\text{d}x-\int \frac{1}{x+1}\,\text{d}x\end{aligned}
$$

For the first integral, we use the substitution ${x}^{2}+5=u.$ Then, $2x\,\text{d}x=\text{d}u,$ and we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{2x}{{x}^{2}+5}\,\text{d}x & =\int \frac{1}{u}\,\text{d}u \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡|u| \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+5).\end{aligned}
$$

For the second integral, we use the fact that $\int \frac{1}{{x}^{2}+{a}^{2}}\,\text{d}x=\frac{1}{a}\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{x}{a}),$ which results in

$$
\begin{aligned}3\int \frac{1}{{x}^{2}+5}\,\text{d}x & =3\int \frac{1}{{x}^{2}+(\sqrt{5})^{2}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{3}{\sqrt{5}}\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{x}{\sqrt{5}}) \\  & =\frac{3\sqrt{5}}{5}\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{\sqrt{5}x}{5}).\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, for the third integral, we get

$$
\int \frac{1}{x+1}\text{d}x=\operatorname{ln}⁡|x+1|.
$$

So, we get the following result:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{{x}^{2}+5x-2}{(x+1)({x}^{2}+5)}\,\text{d}x & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+5)+\frac{3\sqrt{5}}{5}\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{\sqrt{5}x}{5})-\operatorname{ln}⁡|x+1|+C\end{aligned}
$$

Question 6

Find the integral of −x2−7x(x2+6)(x−3).

a
12ln⁡(x2+6)−46arctan⁡(x6)−2ln⁡|x−3|+K
b
 2ln⁡(x2+6)−16arctan⁡(x6)+K
c
 12ln⁡(x2+6)−6arctan⁡(x6)−ln⁡|x−3|+K
d
 ln⁡(x2+6)−46arctan⁡(x6)+K
e
 ln⁡(x2+6)−16arctan⁡(x6)−2ln⁡|x−3|+K
Submit

decision.explanation: The partial fraction decomposition is (x−4)/(x²+6)−2/(x−3), since (x−4)(x−3)−2(x²+6)=−x²−7x. Integrating gives ½ln(x²+6)−(4/√6)arctan(x/√6)−2ln|x−3|+K, matching option a.

after.name: Question 6
after.worked_solution:
The quadratic factor ${x}^{2}+6$ is irreducible, so we proceed with the following partial fraction decomposition:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{-{x}^{2}-7x}{({x}^{2}+6)(x-3)} & =\frac{Ax+B}{{x}^{2}+6}+\frac{C}{x-3}\end{aligned}
$$

To determine the coefficients $A,B,$ and $C,$ we first multiply both sides of the above equation by $({x}^{2}+6)(x-3),$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}-{x}^{2}-7x & =(Ax+B)(x-3)+C({x}^{2}+6).\end{aligned}
$$

Solving for the unknown constants using the usual methods, we get $A=1,B=-4,$ and $C=-2.$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{-{x}^{2}-7x}{({x}^{2}+6)(x-3)} & =\frac{x-4}{{x}^{2}+6}-\frac{2}{x-3}\end{aligned}
$$

We now integrate this function term by term, adding the constant of integration at the very end.

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{-{x}^{2}-7x}{({x}^{2}+6)(x-3)}\,\text{d}x & =\int (\frac{x-4}{{x}^{2}+6}-\frac{2}{x-3})\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\int \frac{2x}{{x}^{2}+6}\,\text{d}x-4\int \frac{1}{{x}^{2}+6}\,\text{d}x-2\int \frac{1}{x-3}\,\text{d}x\end{aligned}
$$

For the first integral, we use the substitution $u={x}^{2}+6.$ Then $\text{d}u=2x\,\text{d}x,$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2}\int \frac{2x}{{x}^{2}+6}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{1}{2}\int \frac{1}{u}\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡|u| \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡|{x}^{2}+6| \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+6).\end{aligned}
$$

For the second integral, we use the fact that $\int \frac{1}{{x}^{2}+{a}^{2}}\,\text{d}x=\frac{1}{a}\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{x}{a}),$ which results in

$$
\int \frac{1}{{x}^{2}+6}\,\text{d}x=\frac{1}{\sqrt{6}}\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{x}{\sqrt{6}}).
$$

Finally, for the third integral, we have

$$
\int \frac{1}{x-3}\,\text{d}x=\operatorname{ln}⁡|x-3|.
$$

So, we get the following result:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{-{x}^{2}-7x}{({x}^{2}+6)(x-3)}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{1}{2}\int \frac{2x}{{x}^{2}+6}\,\text{d}x-4\int \frac{1}{{x}^{2}+6}\,\text{d}x-2\int \frac{1}{x-3}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+6)-\frac{4}{\sqrt{6}}\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{x}{\sqrt{6}})-2\operatorname{ln}⁡|x-3|+K\end{aligned}
$$

Question 6
?

Find the integral of −x2−7x(x2+6)(x−3).

a
12ln⁡(x2+6)−46arctan⁡(x6)−2ln⁡|x−3|+K
b
 2ln⁡(x2+6)−16arctan⁡(x6)+K
c
 12ln⁡(x2+6)−6arctan⁡(x6)−ln⁡|x−3|+K
d
 ln⁡(x2+6)−46arctan⁡(x6)+K
e
 ln⁡(x2+6)−16arctan⁡(x6)−2ln⁡|x−3|+K
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The quadratic factor x2+6 is irreducible, so we proceed with the following partial fraction decomposition: −x2−7x(x2+6)(x−3)=Ax+Bx2+6+Cx−3

To determine the coefficients A,B, and C, we first multiply both sides of the above equation by (x2+6)(x−3), and we get −x2−7x=(Ax+B)(x−3)+C(x2+6).

Solving for the unknown constants using the usual methods, we get A=1,B=−4, and C=−2. Therefore, −x2−7x(x2+6)(x−3)=x−4x2+6−2x−3

We now integrate this function term by term, adding the constant of integration at the very end. ∫−x2−7x(x2+6)(x−3)dx=∫(x−4x2+6−2x−3)dx=12∫2xx2+6dx−4∫1x2+6dx−2∫1x−3dx

For the first integral, we use the substitution u=x2+6. Then du=2xdx, and we get 12∫2xx2+6dx=12∫1udu=12ln⁡|u|=12ln⁡|x2+6|=12ln⁡(x2+6).

For the second integral, we use the fact that ∫1x2+a2dx=1aarctan⁡(xa), which results in ∫1x2+6dx=16arctan⁡(x6).

Finally, for the third integral, we have ∫1x−3dx=ln⁡|x−3|.

So, we get the following result: ∫−x2−7x(x2+6)(x−3)dx=12∫2xx2+6dx−4∫1x2+6dx−2∫1x−3dx=12ln⁡(x2+6)−46arctan⁡(x6)−2ln⁡|x−3|+K

content.knowledge_point: Integrating a Rational Function With an Irreducible Binomial Quadratic Factor
content.worked_solution:
The quadratic factor ${x}^{2}+6$ is irreducible, so we proceed with the following partial fraction decomposition:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{-{x}^{2}-7x}{({x}^{2}+6)(x-3)} & =\frac{Ax+B}{{x}^{2}+6}+\frac{C}{x-3}\end{aligned}
$$

To determine the coefficients $A,B,$ and $C,$ we first multiply both sides of the above equation by $({x}^{2}+6)(x-3),$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}-{x}^{2}-7x & =(Ax+B)(x-3)+C({x}^{2}+6).\end{aligned}
$$

Solving for the unknown constants using the usual methods, we get $A=1,B=-4,$ and $C=-2.$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{-{x}^{2}-7x}{({x}^{2}+6)(x-3)} & =\frac{x-4}{{x}^{2}+6}-\frac{2}{x-3}\end{aligned}
$$

We now integrate this function term by term, adding the constant of integration at the very end.

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{-{x}^{2}-7x}{({x}^{2}+6)(x-3)}\,\text{d}x & =\int (\frac{x-4}{{x}^{2}+6}-\frac{2}{x-3})\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\int \frac{2x}{{x}^{2}+6}\,\text{d}x-4\int \frac{1}{{x}^{2}+6}\,\text{d}x-2\int \frac{1}{x-3}\,\text{d}x\end{aligned}
$$

For the first integral, we use the substitution $u={x}^{2}+6.$ Then $\text{d}u=2x\,\text{d}x,$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2}\int \frac{2x}{{x}^{2}+6}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{1}{2}\int \frac{1}{u}\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡|u| \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡|{x}^{2}+6| \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+6).\end{aligned}
$$

For the second integral, we use the fact that $\int \frac{1}{{x}^{2}+{a}^{2}}\,\text{d}x=\frac{1}{a}\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{x}{a}),$ which results in

$$

$$

The quadratic factor ${x}^{2}+6$ is irreducible, so we proceed with the following partial fraction decomposition:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{-{x}^{2}-7x}{({x}^{2}+6)(x-3)} & =\frac{Ax+B}{{x}^{2}+6}+\frac{C}{x-3}\end{aligned}
$$

To determine the coefficients $A,B,$ and $C,$ we first multiply both sides of the above equation by $({x}^{2}+6)(x-3),$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}-{x}^{2}-7x & =(Ax+B)(x-3)+C({x}^{2}+6).\end{aligned}
$$

Solving for the unknown constants using the usual methods, we get $A=1,B=-4,$ and $C=-2.$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{-{x}^{2}-7x}{({x}^{2}+6)(x-3)} & =\frac{x-4}{{x}^{2}+6}-\frac{2}{x-3}\end{aligned}
$$

We now integrate this function term by term, adding the constant of integration at the very end.

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{-{x}^{2}-7x}{({x}^{2}+6)(x-3)}\,\text{d}x & =\int (\frac{x-4}{{x}^{2}+6}-\frac{2}{x-3})\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\int \frac{2x}{{x}^{2}+6}\,\text{d}x-4\int \frac{1}{{x}^{2}+6}\,\text{d}x-2\int \frac{1}{x-3}\,\text{d}x\end{aligned}
$$

For the first integral, we use the substitution $u={x}^{2}+6.$ Then $\text{d}u=2x\,\text{d}x,$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2}\int \frac{2x}{{x}^{2}+6}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{1}{2}\int \frac{1}{u}\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡|u| \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡|{x}^{2}+6| \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+6).\end{aligned}
$$

For the second integral, we use the fact that $\int \frac{1}{{x}^{2}+{a}^{2}}\,\text{d}x=\frac{1}{a}\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{x}{a}),$ which results in

$$
\int \frac{1}{{x}^{2}+6}\,\text{d}x=\frac{1}{\sqrt{6}}\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{x}{\sqrt{6}}).
$$

Finally, for the third integral, we have

$$
\int \frac{1}{x-3}\,\text{d}x=\operatorname{ln}⁡|x-3|.
$$

So, we get the following result:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{-{x}^{2}-7x}{({x}^{2}+6)(x-3)}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{1}{2}\int \frac{2x}{{x}^{2}+6}\,\text{d}x-4\int \frac{1}{{x}^{2}+6}\,\text{d}x-2\int \frac{1}{x-3}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+6)-\frac{4}{\sqrt{6}}\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{x}{\sqrt{6}})-2\operatorname{ln}⁡|x-3|+K\end{aligned}

Question 7
?

Evaluate ∫3x2+5x−9(x2+3)(x+4)dx.

a
 2ln⁡(x2+3)−3arctan⁡(3x3)+K
b
 ln⁡(x2+3)−3arctan⁡(3x3)+ln⁡|x+4|+K
c
 2ln⁡(x2+3)−33arctan⁡(3x3)+ln⁡|x+4|+K
d
 −ln⁡(x2+3)+3arctan⁡(3x3)+3ln⁡|x+4|+K
e
 ln⁡(x2+3)−33arctan⁡(3x3)+3ln⁡|x+4|+K
Submit

decision.explanation: The integrand decomposes as (2x−3)/(x²+3)+1/(x+4), since (2x−3)(x+4)+(x²+3)=3x²+5x−9. Integrating gives ln(x²+3)−√3 arctan(√3x/3)+ln|x+4|+K, matching option b.

after.name: Question 7
after.worked_solution:
The quadratic factor ${x}^{2}+3$ is irreducible, so we proceed with the following partial fraction decomposition:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{3{x}^{2}+5x-9}{({x}^{2}+3)(x+4)} & =\frac{Ax+B}{{x}^{2}+3}+\frac{C}{x+4}\end{aligned}
$$

To determine the coefficients $A,B,$ and $C,$ we first multiply both sides of the above equation by $({x}^{2}+3)(x+4),$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}3{x}^{2}+5x-9 & =(Ax+B)(x+4)+C({x}^{2}+3).\end{aligned}
$$

Solving for the unknown constants using the usual methods, we get $A=2,B=-3,$ and $C=1.$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{3{x}^{2}+5x-9}{({x}^{2}+3)(x+4)} & =\frac{2x-3}{{x}^{2}+3}+\frac{1}{x+4}\end{aligned}
$$

We now integrate this function term by term, adding the constant of integration at the very end.

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{3{x}^{2}+5x-9}{({x}^{2}+3)(x+4)}\,\text{d}x & =\int (\frac{2x-3}{{x}^{2}+3}+\frac{1}{x+4})\text{d}x \\  & =\int \frac{2x}{{x}^{2}+3}\,\text{d}x-3\int \frac{1}{{x}^{2}+3}\,\text{d}x+\int \frac{1}{x+4}\,\text{d}x\end{aligned}
$$

For the first integral, we use the substitution $u={x}^{2}+3.$ Then $\text{d}u=2x\,\text{d}x,$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{2x}{{x}^{2}+3}\,\text{d}x & =\int \frac{1}{u}\text{d}u \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡|u| \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡|{x}^{2}+3| \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+3).\end{aligned}
$$

For the second integral, we use the fact that $\int \frac{1}{{x}^{2}+{a}^{2}}\,\text{d}x=\frac{1}{a}\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{x}{a}),$ which results in

$$
\begin{aligned}3\int \frac{1}{{x}^{2}+3}\,\text{d}x & =3\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\cdot \operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{x}{\sqrt{3}}) \\  & =\sqrt{3}\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{\sqrt{3}x}{3}).\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, for the third integral, we have

$$
\int \frac{1}{x+4}\,\text{d}x=\operatorname{ln}⁡|x+4|.
$$

So, we get the following result:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{3{x}^{2}+5x-9}{({x}^{2}+3)(x+4)}\,\text{d}x & =\int \frac{2x}{{x}^{2}+3}\,\text{d}x-3\int \frac{1}{{x}^{2}+3}\,\text{d}x+\int \frac{1}{x+4}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+3)-\sqrt{3}\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{\sqrt{3}x}{3})+\operatorname{ln}⁡|x+4|+K\end{aligned}
$$

Evaluate ∫3x2+5x−9(x2+3)(x+4)dx.

a
 2ln⁡(x2+3)−3arctan⁡(3x3)+K
b
 ln⁡(x2+3)−3arctan⁡(3x3)+ln⁡|x+4|+K
c
 2ln⁡(x2+3)−33arctan⁡(3x3)+ln⁡|x+4|+K
d
 −ln⁡(x2+3)+3arctan⁡(3x3)+3ln⁡|x+4|+K
e
 ln⁡(x2+3)−33arctan⁡(3x3)+3ln⁡|x+4|+K
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

The quadratic factor x2+3 is irreducible, so we proceed with the following partial fraction decomposition: 3x2+5x−9(x2+3)(x+4)=Ax+Bx2+3+Cx+4

To determine the coefficients A,B, and C, we first multiply both sides of the above equation by (x2+3)(x+4), and we get 3x2+5x−9=(Ax+B)(x+4)+C(x2+3).

Solving for the unknown constants using the usual methods, we get A=2,B=−3, and C=1. Therefore, 3x2+5x−9(x2+3)(x+4)=2x−3x2+3+1x+4

content.worked_solution:
The quadratic factor ${x}^{2}+3$ is irreducible, so we proceed with the following partial fraction decomposition:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{3{x}^{2}+5x-9}{({x}^{2}+3)(x+4)} & =\frac{Ax+B}{{x}^{2}+3}+\frac{C}{x+4}\end{aligned}
$$

To determine the coefficients $A,B,$ and $C,$ we first multiply both sides of the above equation by $({x}^{2}+3)(x+4),$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}3{x}^{2}+5x-9 & =(Ax+B)(x+4)+C({x}^{2}+3).\end{aligned}
$$

Solving for the unknown constants using the usual methods, we get $A=2,B=-3,$ and $C=1.$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{3{x}^{2}+5x-9}{({x}^{2}+3)(x+4)} & =\frac{2x-3}{{x}^{2}+3}+\frac{1}{x+4}\end{aligned}
$$

We now integrate this function term by term, adding the constant of integration at the very end.

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{3{x}^{2}+5x-9}{({x}^{2}+3)(x+4)}\,\text{d}x & =\int (\frac{2x-3}{{x}^{2}+3}+\frac{1}{x+4})\text{d}x \\  & =\int \frac{2x}{{x}^{2}+3}\,\text{d}x-3\int \frac{1}{{x}^{2}+3}\,\text{d}x+\int \frac{1}{x+4}\,\text{d}x\end{aligned}
$$

For the first integral, we use the substitution $u={x}^{2}+3.$ Then $\text{d}u=2x\,\text{d}x,$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{2x}{{x}^{2}+3}\,\text{d}x & =\int \frac{1}{u}\text{d}u \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡|u| \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡|{x}^{2}+3| \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+3).\end{aligned}
$$

For the second integral, we use the fact that $\int \frac{1}{{x}^{2}+{a}^{2}}\,\text{d}x=\frac{1}{a}\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{x}{a}),$ which results in

$$
\begin{aligned}3\int \frac{1}{{x}^{2}+3}\,\text{d}x & =3\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\cdot \operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{x}{\sqrt{3}}) \\  & =\sqrt{3}\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{\sqrt{3}x}{3}).\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, for the third integral, we have

$$
\int \frac{1}{x+4}\,\text{d}x=\operatorname{ln}⁡|x+4|.
$$

So, we get the following result:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{3{x}^{2}+5x-9}{({x}^{2}+3)(x+4)}\,\text{d}x & =\int \frac{2x}{{x}^{2}+3}\,\text{d}x-3\int \frac{1}{{x}^{2}+3}\,\text{d}x+\int \frac{1}{x+4}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+3)-\sqrt{3}\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{\sqrt{3}x}{3})+\operatorname{ln}⁡|x+4|+K\end{aligned}
$$

Evaluate ∫x2+x+42(x2+9)(x−3)dx.

a
ln⁡(x2+9)+59arctan⁡(x9)+3ln⁡|x−3|+K
b
−ln⁡(x2+9)−53arctan⁡(x3)+3ln⁡|x−3|+K
c
ln⁡(x2+9)−23arctan⁡(x3)−ln⁡|x−3|+K
d

Submit

decision.explanation: The integrand decomposes as (−2x−5)/(x²+9)+3/(x−3), since (−2x−5)(x−3)+3(x²+9)=x²+x+42. Integrating gives −ln(x²+9)−(5/3)arctan(x/3)+3ln|x−3|+K, matching option b.

after.name: Question 8
after.worked_solution:
The quadratic factor ${x}^{2}+9$ is irreducible, so we proceed with the following partial fraction decomposition:

$$
\frac{{x}^{2}+x+42}{({x}^{2}+9)(x-3)}=\frac{Ax+B}{{x}^{2}+9}+\frac{C}{x-3}
$$

To determine the coefficients $A,B,$ and $C,$ we first multiply both sides of the above equation by $({x}^{2}+9)(x-3),$ and we get

$$
{x}^{2}+x+42=(Ax+B)(x-3)+C({x}^{2}+9).
$$

Solving for the unknown constants using the usual methods, we get $A=-2,B=-5,$ and $C=3.$ Therefore,

$$
\frac{{x}^{2}+x+42}{({x}^{2}+9)(x-3)}=-\frac{2x+5}{{x}^{2}+9}+\frac{3}{x-3}.
$$

We now integrate this function term by term, adding the constant of integration at the very end.

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{{x}^{2}+x+42}{({x}^{2}+9)(x-3)}\,\text{d}x & =\int (-\frac{2x+5}{{x}^{2}+9}+\frac{3}{x-3})\text{d}x \\  & =-\int \frac{2x}{{x}^{2}+9}\text{d}x-5\int \frac{1}{{x}^{2}+9}\text{d}x+3\int \frac{1}{x-3}\,\text{d}x\end{aligned}
$$

For the first integral, we use a substitution $u={x}^{2}+9.$ Then $\text{d}u=2x\,\text{d}x,$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{2x}{{x}^{2}+9}\,\text{d}x & =\int (\frac{1}{u})\text{d}u \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡|u| \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡|{x}^{2}+9| \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+9).\end{aligned}
$$

For the second integral, we use the fact that $\int \frac{1}{{x}^{2}+{a}^{2}}\,\text{d}x=\frac{1}{a}\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{x}{a}),$ which results in

$$
\int \frac{1}{{x}^{2}+9}\,\text{d}x=\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{x}{3}).
$$

Finally, for the third integral, we have

$$
\int \frac{1}{x-3}\,\text{d}x=\operatorname{ln}⁡|x-3|.
$$

So, we get the following result:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{{x}^{2}+x+42}{({x}^{2}+9)(x-3)}\,\text{d}x & =-\int \frac{2x}{{x}^{2}+9}\text{d}x-5\int \frac{1}{{x}^{2}+9}\text{d}x+3\int \frac{1}{x-3}\,\text{d}x \\  & =-\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+9)-5\cdot \frac{1}{3}\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{x}{3})+3\cdot \operatorname{ln}⁡|x-3|+K \\  & =-\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+9)-\frac{5}{3}\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{x}{3})+3\operatorname{ln}⁡|x-3|+K\end{aligned}
$$

To determine the coefficients A,B, and C, we first multiply both sides of the above equation by (x2+9)(x−3), and we get x2+x+42=(Ax+B)(x−3)+C(x2+9).

Solving for the unknown constants using the usual methods, we get A=−2,B=−5, and C=3. Therefore, x2+x+42(x2+9)(x−3)=−2x+5x2+9+3x−3.

For the second integral, we use the fact that ∫1x2+a2dx=1aarctan⁡(xa), which results in ∫1x2+9dx=13arctan⁡(x3).

Finally, for the third integral, we have ∫1x−3dx=ln⁡|x−3|.

content.knowledge_point: Integrating a Rational Function With an Irreducible Binomial Quadratic Factor
content.worked_solution:
The quadratic factor ${x}^{2}+9$ is irreducible, so we proceed with the following partial fraction decomposition:

$$
\frac{{x}^{2}+x+42}{({x}^{2}+9)(x-3)}=\frac{Ax+B}{{x}^{2}+9}+\frac{C}{x-3}
$$

To determine the coefficients $A,B,$ and $C,$ we first multiply both sides of the above equation by $({x}^{2}+9)(x-3),$ and we get

$$
{x}^{2}+x+42=(Ax+B)(x-3)+C({x}^{2}+9).
$$

Solving for the unknown constants using the usual methods, we get $A=-2,B=-5,$ and $C=3.$ Therefore,

$$
\frac{{x}^{2}+x+42}{({x}^{2}+9)(x-3)}=-\frac{2x+5}{{x}^{2}+9}+\frac{3}{x-3}.
$$

We now integrate this function term by term, adding the constant of integration at the very end.

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{{x}^{2}+x+42}{({x}^{2}+9)(x-3)}\,\text{d}x & =\int (-\frac{2x+5}{{x}^{2}+9}+\frac{3}{x-3})\text{d}x \\  & =-\int \frac{2x}{{x}^{2}+9}\text{d}x-5\int \frac{1}{{x}^{2}+9}\text{d}x+3\int \frac{1}{x-3}\,\text{d}x\end{aligned}
$$

For the first integral, we use a substitution $u={x}^{2}+9.$ Then $\text{d}u=2x\,\text{d}x,$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{2x}{{x}^{2}+9}\,\text{d}x & =\int (\frac{1}{u})\text{d}u \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡|u| \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡|{x}^{2}+9| \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+9).\end{aligned}
$$

For the second integral, we use the fact that $\int \frac{1}{{x}^{2}+{a}^{2}}\,\text{d}x=\frac{1}{a}\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{x}{a}),$ which results in

$$
\int \frac{1}{{x}^{2}+9}\,\text{d}x=\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{x}{3}).
$$

Finally, for the third integral, we have

$$
\int \frac{1}{x-3}\,\text{d}x=\operatorname{ln}⁡|x-3|.
$$

So, we get the following result:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{{x}^{2}+x+42}{({x}^{2}+9)(x-3)}\,\text{d}x & =-\int \frac{2x}{{x}^{2}+9}\text{d}x-5\int \frac{1}{{x}^{2}+9}\text{d}x+3\int \frac{1}{x-3}\,\text{d}x \\  & =-\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+9)-5\cdot \frac{1}{3}\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{x}{3})+3\cdot \operatorname{ln}⁡|x-3|+K \\  & =-\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+9)-\frac{5}{3}\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{x}{3})+3\operatorname{ln}⁡|x-3|+K\end{aligned}
$$

ln⁡|x−1|−12ln⁡(x2+1)−arctan⁡x+K
b

c

decision.explanation: The integrand decomposes as 1/(x−1)−(x+1)/(x²+1), since (x²+1)−(x+1)(x−1)=2. Integrating gives ln|x−1|−½ln(x²+1)−arctan(x)+K, matching option a.

after.name: Question 9
after.worked_solution:
The quadratic factor ${x}^{2}+1$ is irreducible, so we proceed with the following partial fraction decomposition:

$$
\frac{2}{(x-1)({x}^{2}+1)}=\frac{A}{x-1}+\frac{Bx+C}{{x}^{2}+1}.
$$

To determine the coefficients $A,B,$ and $C,$ we first multiply both sides of the above equation by $(x-1)({x}^{2}+1),$ and we get

$$
2=A({x}^{2}+1)+(Bx+C)(x-1).
$$

Solving for the unknown constants using the usual methods, we get $A=1,B=-1,$ and $C=-1.$ Therefore,

$$
\frac{2}{(x-1)({x}^{2}+1)}=\frac{1}{x-1}+\frac{-x-1}{{x}^{2}+1}.
$$

We now integrate this function term by term, adding the constant of integration at the very end.

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{2}{(x-1)({x}^{2}+1)}\,\text{d}x & =\int (\frac{1}{x-1}+\frac{-x-1}{{x}^{2}+1})\,\text{d}x \\  & =\int \frac{1}{x-1}\,\text{d}x-\int \frac{x}{{x}^{2}+1}\,\text{d}x-\int \frac{1}{{x}^{2}+1}\,\text{d}x\end{aligned}
$$

For the first integral, we have

$$
\int \frac{1}{x-1}\,\text{d}x=\operatorname{ln}⁡|x-1|.
$$

For the second integral, we use the substitution $u={x}^{2}+1.$ Then $\text{d}u=2x\,\text{d}x,$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{x}{{x}^{2}+1}\,\text{d}x & =\int (\frac{1}{u})\frac{\text{d}u}{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡|u| \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡|{x}^{2}+1| \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+1)\,.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, for the third integral, we use the fact that $\int \frac{1}{{x}^{2}+{a}^{2}}\,\text{d}x=\frac{1}{a}\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{x}{a}),$ which results in

$$
\int \frac{1}{{x}^{2}+1}\,\text{d}x=\operatorname{arctan}⁡x.
$$

So, we get the following result:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{2}{(x-1)({x}^{2}+1)}\,\text{d}x & =\int \frac{1}{x-1}\,\text{d}x-\int \frac{x}{{x}^{2}+1}\,\text{d}x-\int \frac{1}{{x}^{2}+1}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡|x-1|-\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+1)-\operatorname{arctan}⁡x+K\end{aligned}
$$

EXPLANATION

The quadratic factor x2+1 is irreducible, so we proceed with the following partial fraction decomposition: 2(x−1)(x2+1)=Ax−1+Bx+Cx2+1.

To determine the coefficients A,B, and C, we first multiply both sides of the above equation by (x−1)(x2+1), and we get 2=A(x2+1)+(Bx+C)(x−1).

Solving for the unknown constants using the usual methods, we get A=1,B=−1, and C=−1. Therefore, 2(x−1)(x2+1)=1x−1+−x−1x2+1.

We now integrate this function term by term, adding the constant of integration at the very end.

∫2(x−1)(x2+1)dx=∫(1x−1+−x−1x2+1)dx=∫1x−1dx−∫xx2+1dx−∫1x2+1dx

For the first integral, we have ∫1x−1dx=ln⁡|x−1|.

For the second integral, we use the substitution u=x2+1. Then du=2xdx, and we get ∫xx2+1dx=∫(1u)du2=12ln⁡|u|=12ln⁡|x2+1|=12ln⁡(x2+1).

Finally, for the third integral, we use the fact that ∫1x2+a2dx=1aarctan⁡(xa), which results in ∫1x2+1dx=arctan⁡x.

So, we get the following result: ∫2(x−1)(x2+1)dx=∫1x−1dx−∫xx2+1dx−∫1x2+1dx=ln⁡|x−1|−12ln⁡(x2+1)−arctan⁡x+K

content.knowledge_point: Integrating a Rational Function With an Irreducible Binomial Quadratic Factor
content.worked_solution:
The quadratic factor ${x}^{2}+1$ is irreducible, so we proceed with the following partial fraction decomposition:

$$
\frac{2}{(x-1)({x}^{2}+1)}=\frac{A}{x-1}+\frac{Bx+C}{{x}^{2}+1}.
$$

To determine the coefficients $A,B,$ and $C,$ we first multiply both sides of the above equation by $(x-1)({x}^{2}+1),$ and we get

$$
2=A({x}^{2}+1)+(Bx+C)(x-1).
$$

Solving for the unknown constants using the usual methods, we get $A=1,B=-1,$ and $C=-1.$ Therefore,

$$
\frac{2}{(x-1)({x}^{2}+1)}=\frac{1}{x-1}+\frac{-x-1}{{x}^{2}+1}.
$$

We now integrate this function term by term, adding the constant of integration at the very end.

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{2}{(x-1)({x}^{2}+1)}\,\text{d}x & =\int (\frac{1}{x-1}+\frac{-x-1}{{x}^{2}+1})\,\text{d}x \\  & =\int \frac{1}{x-1}\,\text{d}x-\int \frac{x}{{x}^{2}+1}\,\text{d}x-\int \frac{1}{{x}^{2}+1}\,\text{d}x\end{aligned}
$$

For the first integral, we have

$$
\int \frac{1}{x-1}\,\text{d}x=\operatorname{ln}⁡|x-1|.
$$

For the second integral, we use the substitution $u={x}^{2}+1.$ Then $\text{d}u=2x\,\text{d}x,$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{x}{{x}^{2}+1}\,\text{d}x & =\int (\frac{1}{u})\frac{\text{d}u}{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡|u| \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡|{x}^{2}+1| \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+1)\,.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, for the third integral, we use the fact that $\int \frac{1}{{x}^{2}+{a}^{2}}\,\text{d}x=\frac{1}{a}\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{x}{a}),$ which results in

$$
\int \frac{1}{{x}^{2}+1}\,\text{d}x=\operatorname{arctan}⁡x.
$$

So, we get the following result:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{2}{(x-1)({x}^{2}+1)}\,\text{d}x & =\int \frac{1}{x-1}\,\text{d}x-\int \frac{x}{{x}^{2}+1}\,\text{d}x-\int \frac{1}{{x}^{2}+1}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡|x-1|-\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+1)-\operatorname{arctan}⁡x+K\end{aligned}
$$

Question 10
?

Calculate the integral of x2+4x+12(x−2)(x2+4).

a
3ln⁡|x−2|−2ln⁡|x+4|+4x+4+K
b
3ln⁡|x−2|+13ln⁡(x2+4)+K
c
2ln⁡|x−2|−4ln⁡(x2+4)+K
d
3ln⁡|x−2|−ln⁡(x2+4)+K
e
2ln⁡|x−2|−4ln⁡|x+4|−1x+4+K
Submit

decision.explanation: The integrand decomposes as 3/(x−2)−2x/(x²+4), since 3(x²+4)−2x(x−2)=x²+4x+12. Integrating gives 3ln|x−2|−ln(x²+4)+K, matching option d.

after.name: Question 10
after.worked_solution:
The quadratic factor ${x}^{2}+4$ is irreducible, so we proceed with the following partial fraction decomposition:

$$
\frac{{x}^{2}+4x+12}{(x-2)({x}^{2}+4)}=\frac{A}{x-2}+\frac{Bx+C}{{x}^{2}+4}
$$

To determine the coefficients $A,B,$ and $C,$ we first multiply both sides of the above equation by $(x-2)({x}^{2}+4),$ and we get

$$
{x}^{2}+4x+12=A({x}^{2}+4)+(Bx+C)(x-2).
$$

Solving for the unknown constants using the usual methods, we get $A=3,B=-2,$ and $C=0.$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{x}^{2}+4x+12}{(x-2)({x}^{2}+4)} & =\frac{3}{x-2}+\frac{-2x+0}{{x}^{2}+4} \\  & =\frac{3}{x-2}-\frac{2x}{{x}^{2}+4}.\end{aligned}
$$

We now integrate this function term by term, adding the constant of integration at the very end.

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{{x}^{2}+4x+12}{(x-2)({x}^{2}+4)}\,\text{d}x & =\int (\frac{3}{x-2}-\frac{2x}{{x}^{2}+4})\text{d}x \\  & =3\int \frac{1}{x-2}\,\text{d}x-\int \frac{2x}{{x}^{2}+4}\,\text{d}x\end{aligned}
$$

For the first integral, we have

$$
\int \frac{1}{x-2}\,\text{d}x=\operatorname{ln}⁡|x-2|.
$$

             

For the second integral, we use the substitution $u={x}^{2}+4.$ Then $\text{d}u=2x\,\text{d}x,$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{2x}{{x}^{2}+4}\,\text{d}x & =\int \frac{1}{u}\cdot \text{d}u \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡|u| \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡|{x}^{2}+4| \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+4).\end{aligned}
$$

So, we get the following result:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{{x}^{2}+4x+12}{(x-2)({x}^{2}+4)}\,\text{d}x & =3\int \frac{1}{x-2}\,\text{d}x-\int \frac{2x}{{x}^{2}+4}\,\text{d}x \\  & =3\operatorname{ln}⁡|x-2|-\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+4)+K\end{aligned}
$$

Question 10
?

Calculate the integral of x2+4x+12(x−2)(x2+4).

a
3ln⁡|x−2|−2ln⁡|x+4|+4x+4+K
b
3ln⁡|x−2|+13ln⁡(x2+4)+K
c
2ln⁡|x−2|−4ln⁡(x2+4)+K
d
3ln⁡|x−2|−ln⁡(x2+4)+K
e
2ln⁡|x−2|−4ln⁡|x+4|−1x+4+K
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The quadratic factor x2+4 is irreducible, so we proceed with the following partial fraction decomposition: x2+4x+12(x−2)(x2+4)=Ax−2+Bx+Cx2+4

To determine the coefficients A,B, and C, we first multiply both sides of the above equation by (x−2)(x2+4), and we get x2+4x+12=A(x2+4)+(Bx+C)(x−2).

Solving for the unknown constants using the usual methods, we get A=3,B=−2, and C=0. Therefore, x2+4x+12(x−2)(x2+4)=3x−2+−2x+0x2+4=3x−2−2xx2+4.

We now integrate this function term by term, adding the constant of integration at the very end. ∫x2+4x+12(x−2)(x2+4)dx=∫(3x−2−2xx2+4)dx=3∫1x−2dx−∫2xx2+4dx

For the first integral, we have ∫1x−2dx=ln⁡|x−2|.

For the second integral, we use the substitution u=x2+4. Then du=2xdx, and we get ∫2xx2+4dx=∫1u⋅du=ln⁡|u|=ln⁡|x2+4|=ln⁡(x2+4).

So, we get the following result: ∫x2+4x+12(x−2)(x2+4)dx=3∫1x−2dx−∫2xx2+4dx=3ln⁡|x−2|−ln⁡(x2+4)+K

content.knowledge_point: Integrating a Rational Function With an Irreducible Binomial Quadratic Factor
content.worked_solution:
The quadratic factor ${x}^{2}+4$ is irreducible, so we proceed with the following partial fraction decomposition:

$$
\frac{{x}^{2}+4x+12}{(x-2)({x}^{2}+4)}=\frac{A}{x-2}+\frac{Bx+C}{{x}^{2}+4}
$$

To determine the coefficients $A,B,$ and $C,$ we first multiply both sides of the above equation by $(x-2)({x}^{2}+4),$ and we get

$$
{x}^{2}+4x+12=A({x}^{2}+4)+(Bx+C)(x-2).
$$

Solving for the unknown constants using the usual methods, we get $A=3,B=-2,$ and $C=0.$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{x}^{2}+4x+12}{(x-2)({x}^{2}+4)} & =\frac{3}{x-2}+\frac{-2x+0}{{x}^{2}+4} \\  & =\frac{3}{x-2}-\frac{2x}{{x}^{2}+4}.\end{aligned}
$$

We now integrate this function term by term, adding the constant of integration at the very end.

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{{x}^{2}+4x+12}{(x-2)({x}^{2}+4)}\,\text{d}x & =\int (\frac{3}{x-2}-\frac{2x}{{x}^{2}+4})\text{d}x \\  & =3\int \frac{1}{x-2}\,\text{d}x-\int \frac{2x}{{x}^{2}+4}\,\text{d}x\end{aligned}
$$

For the first integral, we have

$$
\int \frac{1}{x-2}\,\text{d}x=\operatorname{ln}⁡|x-2|.
$$

             

For the second integral, we use the substitution $u={x}^{2}+4.$ Then $\text{d}u=2x\,\text{d}x,$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{2x}{{x}^{2}+4}\,\text{d}x & =\int \frac{1}{u}\cdot \text{d}u \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡|u| \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡|{x}^{2}+4| \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+4).\end{aligned}
$$

So, we get the following result:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{{x}^{2}+4x+12}{(x-2)({x}^{2}+4)}\,\text{d}x & =3\int \frac{1}{x-2}\,\text{d}x-\int \frac{2x}{{x}^{2}+4}\,\text{d}x \\  & =3\operatorname{ln}⁡|x-2|-\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+4)+K\end{aligned}
$$

before.html:
Question 11
?

Calculate ∫3x2+2x+1x(x2+x+1)dx.

a
2ln⁡|x|−3ln⁡(x2+x+1)+K
b
3ln⁡|x|−ln⁡(x2+x+1)+K
c
2ln⁡|x|+5ln⁡(x2+x+1)+K
d
ln⁡|x|+ln⁡(x2+x+1)+K
e
ln⁡|x|+2ln⁡(x2+x+1)+K
Submit

decision.explanation: The integrand equals 1/x+(2x+1)/(x²+x+1), because (x²+x+1)+x(2x+1)=3x²+2x+1. Integrating gives ln|x|+ln(x²+x+1)+K, matching option d. The quadratic is always positive since x²+x+1=(x+½)²+¾.

after.name: Question 11
after.worked_solution:
Notice that the quadratic factor in the denominator has a negative discriminant:

$$
D={1}^{2}-4(1)(1)=-3<0
$$

So, we proceed with the following partial fraction decomposition:

$$
\frac{3{x}^{2}+2x+1}{x({x}^{2}+x+1)}=\frac{A}{x}+\frac{Bx+C}{{x}^{2}+x+1}
$$

To determine the coefficients $A,B,$ and $C,$ we first multiply both sides of the above equation by $x({x}^{2}+x+1),$ and we get

$$
3{x}^{2}+2x+1=A({x}^{2}+x+1)+(Bx+C)x.
$$

Solving for the unknown constants using the usual methods, we get $A=1,B=2,$ and $C=1.$ Therefore,

$$
\frac{3{x}^{2}+2x+1}{x({x}^{2}+x+1)}=\frac{1}{x}+\frac{2x+1}{{x}^{2}+x+1}.
$$

We now integrate this function term by term, adding the constant of integration at the very end.

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{3{x}^{2}+2x+1}{x({x}^{2}+x+1)}\,\text{d}x & =\int (\frac{1}{x}+\frac{2x+1}{{x}^{2}+x+1})\text{d}x \\  & =\int \frac{1}{x}\,\text{d}x+\int \frac{2x+1}{{x}^{2}+x+1}\,\text{d}x\end{aligned}
$$

For the first integral, we have

$$
\int \frac{1}{x}\,\text{d}x=\operatorname{ln}⁡|x|.
$$

For the second integral, we use the substitution $u={x}^{2}+x+1.$ Then $\text{d}u=(2x+1)\,\text{d}x,$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{2x+1}{{x}^{2}+x+1}\,\text{d}x & =\int (\frac{1}{u})\text{d}u \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡|u| \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡|{x}^{2}+x+1| \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+x+1).\end{aligned}
$$

So, we get the following result:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{3{x}^{2}+2x+1}{x({x}^{2}+x+1)}\,\text{d}x & =\int \frac{1}{x}\,\text{d}x+\int \frac{2x+1}{{x}^{2}+x+1}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡|x|+\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+x+1)+K\end{aligned}
$$

Question 11
?

Calculate ∫3x2+2x+1x(x2+x+1)dx.

a
2ln⁡|x|−3ln⁡(x2+x+1)+K
b
3ln⁡|x|−ln⁡(x2+x+1)+K
c
2ln⁡|x|+5ln⁡(x2+x+1)+K
d
ln⁡|x|+ln⁡(x2+x+1)+K
e
ln⁡|x|+2ln⁡(x2+x+1)+K
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Notice that the quadratic factor in the denominator has a negative discriminant: D=12−4(1)(1)=−3<0

So, we proceed with the following partial fraction decomposition: 3x2+2x+1x(x2+x+1)=Ax+Bx+Cx2+x+1

To determine the coefficients A,B, and C, we first multiply both sides of the above equation by x(x2+x+1), and we get 3x2+2x+1=A(x2+x+1)+(Bx+C)x.

Solving for the unknown constants using the usual methods, we get A=1,B=2, and C=1. Therefore, 3x2+2x+1x(x2+x+1)=1x+2x+1x2+x+1.

We now integrate this function term by term, adding the constant of integration at the very end. ∫3x2+2x+1x(x2+x+1)dx=∫(1x+2x+1x2+x+1)dx=∫1xdx+∫2x+1x2+x+1dx

For the first integral, we have ∫1xdx=ln⁡|x|.

For the second integral, we use the substitution u=x2+x+1. Then du=(2x+1)dx, and we get ∫2x+1x2+x+1dx=∫(1u)du=ln⁡|u|=ln⁡|x2+x+1|=ln⁡(x2+x+1).

So, we get the following result: ∫3x2+2x+1x(x2+x+1)dx=∫1xdx+∫2x+1x2+x+1dx=ln⁡|x|+ln⁡(x2+x+1)+K

content.knowledge_point: Integrating a Rational Function With an Irreducible Trinomial Quadratic Factor
content.worked_solution:
Notice that the quadratic factor in the denominator has a negative discriminant:

$$
D={1}^{2}-4(1)(1)=-3<0
$$

So, we proceed with the following partial fraction decomposition:

$$
\frac{3{x}^{2}+2x+1}{x({x}^{2}+x+1)}=\frac{A}{x}+\frac{Bx+C}{{x}^{2}+x+1}
$$

To determine the coefficients $A,B,$ and $C,$ we first multiply both sides of the above equation by $x({x}^{2}+x+1),$ and we get

$$
3{x}^{2}+2x+1=A({x}^{2}+x+1)+(Bx+C)x.
$$

Solving for the unknown constants using the usual methods, we get $A=1,B=2,$ and $C=1.$ Therefore,

$$
\frac{3{x}^{2}+2x+1}{x({x}^{2}+x+1)}=\frac{1}{x}+\frac{2x+1}{{x}^{2}+x+1}.
$$

We now integrate this function term by term, adding the constant of integration at the very end.

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{3{x}^{2}+2x+1}{x({x}^{2}+x+1)}\,\text{d}x & =\int (\frac{1}{x}+\frac{2x+1}{{x}^{2}+x+1})\text{d}x \\  & =\int \frac{1}{x}\,\text{d}x+\int \frac{2x+1}{{x}^{2}+x+1}\,\text{d}x\end{aligned}
$$

For the first integral, we have

$$
\int \frac{1}{x}\,\text{d}x=\operatorname{ln}⁡|x|.
$$

For the second integral, we use the substitution $u={x}^{2}+x+1.$ Then $\text{d}u=(2x+1)\,\text{d}x,$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{2x+1}{{x}^{2}+x+1}\,\text{d}x & =\int (\frac{1}{u})\text{d}u \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡|u| \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡|{x}^{2}+x+1| \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+x+1).\end{aligned}
$$

So, we get the following result:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{3{x}^{2}+2x+1}{x({x}^{2}+x+1)}\,\text{d}x & =\int \frac{1}{x}\,\text{d}x+\int \frac{2x+1}{{x}^{2}+x+1}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡|x|+\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+x+1)+K\end{aligned}
$$

before.html:
Question 12
?

∫3x2+9x−4(x−1)(x2+4x−1)dx=

a
2ln⁡|x−1|−ln⁡|x2+4x−1|+K
b
2ln⁡|x2+4x−1|+2x−1+K
c
2ln⁡|x−1|+12ln⁡|x2+4x−1|+K
d
2ln⁡|x2+4x−1|+12x−2+K
e
12ln⁡|x2+4x−1|+2x−1+K
Submit

decision.explanation: The integrand equals 2/(x−1)+(x+2)/(x²+4x−1), since 2(x²+4x−1)+(x+2)(x−1)=3x²+9x−4. As x+2 is half the derivative of the quadratic, integration gives 2ln|x−1|+½ln|x²+4x−1|+K, matching option c.

after.name: Question 12
after.worked_solution:
Notice that the quadratic factor in the denominator has a discriminant that is not a perfect square:

$$
D={4}^{2}-4(1)(-1)=20
$$

We have that $\sqrt{20}$ is not a rational number, which implies that the quadratic factor doesn't factor over the rational numbers.

So, we proceed with the following partial fraction decomposition:

$$
\frac{3{x}^{2}+9x-4}{(x-1)({x}^{2}+4x-1)}=\frac{A}{x-1}+\frac{Bx+C}{{x}^{2}+4x-1}
$$

To determine the coefficients $A,B,$ and $C,$ we first multiply both sides of the above equation by $(x-1)({x}^{2}+4x-1),$ and we get

$$
3{x}^{2}+9x-4=A({x}^{2}+4x-1)+(Bx+C)(x-1)
$$

Solving for the unknown constants using the usual methods, we get $A=2,B=1$ and $C=2.$ Therefore,

$$
\frac{3{x}^{2}+9x-4}{(x-1)({x}^{2}+4x-1)}=\frac{2}{x-1}+\frac{x+2}{{x}^{2}+4x-1}.
$$

We now integrate this function term by term, adding the constant of integration at the very end.

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{3{x}^{2}+9x-4}{(x-1)({x}^{2}+4x-1)}\,\text{d}x & =\int (\frac{2}{x-1}+\frac{x+2}{{x}^{2}+4x-1})\,\text{d}x \\  & =2\int \frac{1}{x-1}\,\text{d}x+\int \frac{x+2}{{x}^{2}+4x-1}\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

For the first integral, we have

$$
2\int \frac{1}{x-1}\,\text{d}x=2\operatorname{ln}⁡|x-1|.
$$

For the second integral, we use the substitution $u={x}^{2}+4x-1.$ Then $\text{d}u=2(x+2)\,\text{d}x,$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{x+2}{{x}^{2}+4x-1}\,\text{d}x & =\int (\frac{1}{u})\frac{\text{d}u}{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡|u| \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡|{x}^{2}+4x-1|.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we get the following result:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{3{x}^{2}+9x-4}{(x-1)({x}^{2}+4x-1)}\,\text{d}x & =2\int \frac{1}{x-1}\,\text{d}x+\int \frac{x+2}{{x}^{2}+4x-1}\,\text{d}x \\  & =2\operatorname{ln}⁡|x-1|+\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡|{x}^{2}+4x-1|+K.\end{aligned}
$$

∫3x2+9x−4(x−1)(x2+4x−1)dx=

a
2ln⁡|x−1|−ln⁡|x2+4x−1|+K
b
2ln⁡|x2+4x−1|+2x−1+K
c
2ln⁡|x−1|+12ln⁡|x2+4x−1|+K
d
2ln⁡|x2+4x−1|+12x−2+K
e
12ln⁡|x2+4x−1|+2x−1+K
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

Notice that the quadratic factor in the denominator has a discriminant that is not a perfect square: D=42−4(1)(−1)=20

We have that 20 is not a rational number, which implies that the quadratic factor doesn't factor over the rational numbers.

So, we proceed with the following partial fraction decomposition: 3x2+9x−4(x−1)(x2+4x−1)=Ax−1+Bx+Cx2+4x−1

To determine the coefficients A,B, and C, we first multiply both sides of the above equation by (x−1)(x2+4x−1), and we get

3x2+9x−4=A(x2+4x−1)+(Bx+C)(x−1)

Solving for the unknown constants using the usual methods, we get A=2,B=1 and C=2. Therefore, 3x2+9x−4(x−1)(x2+4x−1)=2x−1+x+2x2+4x−1.

We now integrate this function term by term, adding the constant of integration at the very end.

∫3x2+9x−4(x−1)(x2+4x−1)dx=∫(2x−1+x+2x2+4x−1)dx=2∫1x−1dx+∫x+2x2+4x−1dx.

For the first integral, we have 2∫1x−1dx=2ln⁡|x−1|.

content.knowledge_point: Integrating a Rational Function With an Irreducible Trinomial Quadratic Factor
content.worked_solution:
Notice that the quadratic factor in the denominator has a discriminant that is not a perfect square:

$$
D={4}^{2}-4(1)(-1)=20
$$

We have that $\sqrt{20}$ is not a rational number, which implies that the quadratic factor doesn't factor over the rational numbers.

So, we proceed with the following partial fraction decomposition:

$$
\frac{3{x}^{2}+9x-4}{(x-1)({x}^{2}+4x-1)}=\frac{A}{x-1}+\frac{Bx+C}{{x}^{2}+4x-1}
$$

To determine the coefficients $A,B,$ and $C,$ we first multiply both sides of the above equation by $(x-1)({x}^{2}+4x-1),$ and we get

$$
3{x}^{2}+9x-4=A({x}^{2}+4x-1)+(Bx+C)(x-1)
$$

Solving for the unknown constants using the usual methods, we get $A=2,B=1$ and $C=2.$ Therefore,

$$
\frac{3{x}^{2}+9x-4}{(x-1)({x}^{2}+4x-1)}=\frac{2}{x-1}+\frac{x+2}{{x}^{2}+4x-1}.
$$

We now integrate this function term by term, adding the constant of integration at the very end.

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{3{x}^{2}+9x-4}{(x-1)({x}^{2}+4x-1)}\,\text{d}x & =\int (\frac{2}{x-1}+\frac{x+2}{{x}^{2}+4x-1})\,\text{d}x \\  & =2\int \frac{1}{x-1}\,\text{d}x+\int \frac{x+2}{{x}^{2}+4x-1}\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

For the first integral, we have

$$
2\int \frac{1}{x-1}\,\text{d}x=2\operatorname{ln}⁡|x-1|.
$$

For the second integral, we use the substitution $u={x}^{2}+4x-1.$ Then $\text{d}u=2(x+2)\,\text{d}x,$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{x+2}{{x}^{2}+4x-1}\,\text{d}x & =\int (\frac{1}{u})\frac{\text{d}u}{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡|u| \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡|{x}^{2}+4x-1|.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we get the following result:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{3{x}^{2}+9x-4}{(x-1)({x}^{2}+4x-1)}\,\text{d}x & =2\int \frac{1}{x-1}\,\text{d}x+\int \frac{x+2}{{x}^{2}+4x-1}\,\text{d}x \\  & =2\operatorname{ln}⁡|x-1|+\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡|{x}^{2}+4x-1|+K.\end{aligned}
$$

Calculate ∫4x2−3x+4x(x2−x+2)dx.

a
 2ln⁡|x|+ln⁡(x2−x+2)+K
b
 ln⁡|x|+12ln⁡(x2−x+2)+K
c
 2ln⁡|x|+1x2−x+2+K
d
 12ln⁡|x|+2x2−x+2+K
e
 ln⁡|x|−2ln⁡(x2−x+2)+K
Submit

decision.explanation: The integrand equals 2/x+(2x−1)/(x²−x+2), since 2(x²−x+2)+x(2x−1)=4x²−3x+4. Integrating gives 2ln|x|+ln(x²−x+2)+K, matching option a. The quadratic is positive for all real x.

after.name: Question 13
after.worked_solution:
Notice that the quadratic factor in the denominator has a negative discriminant:

$$
D=(-1)^{2}-4(1)(2)=-7<0
$$

So, we proceed with the following partial fraction decomposition:

$$
\frac{4{x}^{2}-3x+4}{x({x}^{2}-x+2)}=\frac{A}{x}+\frac{Bx+C}{{x}^{2}-x+2}
$$

To determine the coefficients $A,B,$ and $C,$ we first multiply both sides of the above equation by $x({x}^{2}-x+2),$ and we get

$$
4{x}^{2}-3x+4=A({x}^{2}-x+2)+(Bx+C)x.
$$

Solving for the unknown constants using the usual methods, we get $A=2,B=2,$ and $C=-1.$ Therefore,

$$
\frac{4{x}^{2}-3x+4}{x({x}^{2}-x+2)}=\frac{2}{x}+\frac{2x-1}{{x}^{2}-x+2}.
$$

We now integrate this function term by term, adding the constant of integration at the very end.

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{4{x}^{2}-3x+4}{x({x}^{2}-x+2)}\,\text{d}x & =\int (\frac{2}{x}+\frac{2x-1}{{x}^{2}-x+2})\text{d}x \\  & =2\int \frac{1}{x}\,\text{d}x+\int \frac{2x-1}{{x}^{2}-x+2}\,\text{d}x\end{aligned}
$$

For the first integral, we have

$$
\int \frac{1}{x}\,\text{d}x=\operatorname{ln}⁡|x|.
$$

For the second integral, we use the substitution $u={x}^{2}-x+2.$ Then $\text{d}u=(2x-1)\,\text{d}x,$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{2x-1}{{x}^{2}-x+2}\,\text{d}x & =\int (\frac{1}{u})\text{d}u \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡|u| \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡|{x}^{2}-x+2| \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}-x+2).\end{aligned}
$$

So, we get the following result:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{4{x}^{2}-3x+4}{x({x}^{2}-x+2)}\,\text{d}x & =2\int \frac{1}{x}\,\text{d}x+\int \frac{2x-1}{{x}^{2}-x+2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =2\operatorname{ln}⁡|x|+\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}-x+2)+K\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that the quadratic factor in the denominator has a negative discriminant:

$$
D=(-1)^{2}-4(1)(2)=-7<0
$$

So, we proceed with the following partial fraction decomposition:

$$
\frac{4{x}^{2}-3x+4}{x({x}^{2}-x+2)}=\frac{A}{x}+\frac{Bx+C}{{x}^{2}-x+2}
$$

To determine the coefficients $A,B,$ and $C,$ we first multiply both sides of the above equation by $x({x}^{2}-x+2),$ and we get

$$
4{x}^{2}-3x+4=A({x}^{2}-x+2)+(Bx+C)x.
$$

Solving for the unknown constants using the usual methods, we get $A=2,B=2,$ and $C=-1.$ Therefore,

$$
\frac{4{x}^{2}-3x+4}{x({x}^{2}-x+2)}=\frac{2}{x}+\frac{2x-1}{{x}^{2}-x+2}.
$$

We now integrate this function term by term, adding the constant of integration at the very end.

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{4{x}^{2}-3x+4}{x({x}^{2}-x+2)}\,\text{d}x & =\int (\frac{2}{x}+\frac{2x-1}{{x}^{2}-x+2})\text{d}x \\  & =2\int \frac{1}{x}\,\text{d}x+\int \frac{2x-1}{{x}^{2}-x+2}\,\text{d}x\end{aligned}
$$

For the first integral, we have

$$
\int \frac{1}{x}\,\text{d}x=\operatorname{ln}⁡|x|.
$$

For the second integral, we use the substitution $u={x}^{2}-x+2.$ Then $\text{d}u=(2x-1)\,\text{d}x,$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{2x-1}{{x}^{2}-x+2}\,\text{d}x & =\int (\frac{1}{u})\text{d}u \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡|u| \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡|{x}^{2}-x+2| \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}-x+2).\end{aligned}
$$

So, we get the following result:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{4{x}^{2}-3x+4}{x({x}^{2}-x+2)}\,\text{d}x & =2\int \frac{1}{x}\,\text{d}x+\int \frac{2x-1}{{x}^{2}-x+2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =2\operatorname{ln}⁡|x|+\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}-x+2)+K\end{aligned}
$$

Question 14
?

Evaluate ∫15−25x(2x2−6x+9)(x−4)dx.

a
52ln⁡(2x2−6x+9)−5ln⁡|x−4|+K
b
5ln⁡(2x2−6x+9)−5ln⁡|x−4|+K
c
25ln⁡(2x2−6x+9)−10ln⁡|x−4|+K
d
5ln⁡|x−4|−25ln⁡(2x2−6x+9)+K
e
52ln⁡|x−4|+25ln⁡(2x2−6x+9)+K
Submit

decision.explanation: The integrand equals (10x−15)/(2x²−6x+9)−5/(x−4), since (10x−15)(x−4)−5(2x²−6x+9)=15−25x. The first numerator is 5/2 times the quadratic's derivative. Thus the integral is (5/2)ln(2x²−6x+9)−5ln|x−4|+K, matching option a.

after.name: Question 14
after.worked_solution:
Notice that the quadratic factor in the denominator has a negative discriminant:

$$
D=(-6)^{2}-4(2)(9)=-36<0
$$

So, we proceed with the following partial fraction decomposition:

$$
\frac{15-25x}{(2{x}^{2}-6x+9)(x-4)}=\frac{Ax+B}{2{x}^{2}-6x+9}+\frac{C}{x-4}
$$

To determine the coefficients $A,B,$ and $C,$ we first multiply both sides of the above equation by $(2{x}^{2}-6x+9)(x-4),$ and we get

$$
15-25x=(Ax+B)(x-4)+C(2{x}^{2}-6x+9).
$$

Solving for the unknown constants using the usual methods, we get $A=10,B=-15$ and $C=-5.$ Therefore,

$$
\frac{15-25x}{(2{x}^{2}-6x+9)(x-4)}=\frac{10x-15}{2{x}^{2}-6x+9}+\frac{-5}{x-4}.
$$

We now integrate this function term by term, adding the constant of integration at the very end.

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{15-25x}{(2{x}^{2}-6x+9)(x-4)}\,\text{d}x & =\int (\frac{10x-15}{2{x}^{2}-6x+9}+\frac{-5}{x-4})\,\text{d}x \\  & =5\int \frac{2x-3}{2{x}^{2}-6x+9}\,\text{d}x-5\int \frac{1}{x-4}\,\text{d}x\end{aligned}
$$

For the first integral, we use the substitution $u=2{x}^{2}-6x+9.$ Then $\text{d}u=(4x-6)\,\text{d}x,$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{2x-3}{2{x}^{2}-6x+9}\,\text{d}x & =\int (\frac{1}{u})\frac{\text{d}u}{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡|u| \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡|2{x}^{2}-6x+9| \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡(2{x}^{2}-6x+9).\end{aligned}
$$

For the second integral, we have

$$
\int \frac{1}{x-4}\,\text{d}x=\operatorname{ln}⁡|x-4|.
$$

So, we get the following result:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{15-25x}{(2{x}^{2}-6x+9)(x-4)}\,\text{d}x & =5\int \frac{2x-3}{2{x}^{2}-6x+9}\,\text{d}x-5\int \frac{1}{x-4}\,\text{d}x \\  & =5(\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡(2{x}^{2}-6x+9))-5\operatorname{ln}⁡|x-4|+K \\  & =\frac{5}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡(2{x}^{2}-6x+9)-5\operatorname{ln}⁡|x-4|+K\end{aligned}
$$
