Question 14
?

Evaluate ∫15−25x(2x2−6x+9)(x−4)dx.

a
52ln⁡(2x2−6x+9)−5ln⁡|x−4|+K
b
5ln⁡(2x2−6x+9)−5ln⁡|x−4|+K
c
25ln⁡(2x2−6x+9)−10ln⁡|x−4|+K
d
5ln⁡|x−4|−25ln⁡(2x2−6x+9)+K
e
52ln⁡|x−4|+25ln⁡(2x2−6x+9)+K
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

Notice that the quadratic factor in the denominator has a negative discriminant: D=(−6)2−4(2)(9)=−36<0

So, we proceed with the following partial fraction decomposition: 15−25x(2x2−6x+9)(x−4)=Ax+B2x2−6x+9+Cx−4

To determine the coefficients A,B, and C, we first multiply both sides of the above equation by (2x2−6x+9)(x−4), and we get 15−25x=(Ax+B)(x−4)+C(2x2−6x+9).

Solving for the unknown constants using the usual methods, we get A=10,B=−15 and C=−5. Therefore, 15−25x(2x2−6x+9)(x−4)=10x−152x2−6x+9+−5x−4.

We now integrate this function term by term, adding the constant of integration at the very end.

∫15−25x(2x2−6x+9)(x−4)dx=∫(10x−152x2−6x+9+−5x−4)dx=5∫2x−32x2−6x+9dx−5∫1x−4dx

For the first integral, we use the substitution u=2x2−6x+9. Then du=(4x−6)dx, and we get ∫2x−32x2−6x+9dx=∫(1u)du2=12ln⁡|u|=12ln⁡|2x2−6x+9|=12ln⁡(2x2−6x+9).

For the second integral, we have ∫1x−4dx=ln⁡|x−4|.

So, we get the following result: ∫15−25x(2x2−6x+9)(x−4)dx=5∫2x−32x2−6x+9dx−5∫1x−4dx=5(12ln⁡(2x2−6x+9))−5ln⁡|x−4|+K=52ln⁡(2x2−6x+9)−5ln⁡|x−4|+K

verification.explanation: The revealed solution confirms option a. Its derivative is (10x−15)/(2x²−6x+9)−5/(x−4), which combines to (15−25x)/((2x²−6x+9)(x−4)), exactly the integrand. The incorrect feedback concerns the deliberately submitted option c.

content.knowledge_point: Integrating a Rational Function With an Irreducible Trinomial Quadratic Factor
content.worked_solution:
Notice that the quadratic factor in the denominator has a negative discriminant:

$$
D=(-6)^{2}-4(2)(9)=-36<0
$$

So, we proceed with the following partial fraction decomposition:

$$
\frac{15-25x}{(2{x}^{2}-6x+9)(x-4)}=\frac{Ax+B}{2{x}^{2}-6x+9}+\frac{C}{x-4}
$$

To determine the coefficients $A,B,$ and $C,$ we first multiply both sides of the above equation by $(2{x}^{2}-6x+9)(x-4),$ and we get

$$
15-25x=(Ax+B)(x-4)+C(2{x}^{2}-6x+9).
$$

Solving for the unknown constants using the usual methods, we get $A=10,B=-15$ and $C=-5.$ Therefore,

$$
\frac{15-25x}{(2{x}^{2}-6x+9)(x-4)}=\frac{10x-15}{2{x}^{2}-6x+9}+\frac{-5}{x-4}.
$$

We now integrate this function term by term, adding the constant of integration at the very end.

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{15-25x}{(2{x}^{2}-6x+9)(x-4)}\,\text{d}x & =\int (\frac{10x-15}{2{x}^{2}-6x+9}+\frac{-5}{x-4})\,\text{d}x \\  & =5\int \frac{2x-3}{2{x}^{2}-6x+9}\,\text{d}x-5\int \frac{1}{x-4}\,\text{d}x\end{aligned}
$$

For the first integral, we use the substitution $u=2{x}^{2}-6x+9.$ Then $\text{d}u=(4x-6)\,\text{d}x,$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{2x-3}{2{x}^{2}-6x+9}\,\text{d}x & =\int (\frac{1}{u})\frac{\text{d}u}{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡|u| \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡|2{x}^{2}-6x+9| \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡(2{x}^{2}-6x+9).\end{aligned}
$$

For the second integral, we have

$$
\int \frac{1}{x-4}\,\text{d}x=\operatorname{ln}⁡|x-4|.
$$

So, we get the following result:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{15-25x}{(2{x}^{2}-6x+9)(x-4)}\,\text{d}x & =5\int \frac{2x-3}{2{x}^{2}-6x+9}\,\text{d}x-5\int \frac{1}{x-4}\,\text{d}x \\  & =5(\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡(2{x}^{2}-6x+9))-5\operatorname{ln}⁡|x-4|+K \\  & =\frac{5}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡(2{x}^{2}-6x+9)-5\operatorname{ln}⁡|x-4|+K\end{aligned}
$$

Question 15
?

Evaluate the integral ∫12−5xx(2x2+5x−6)dx.

a
 −2ln⁡|x|+ln⁡|2x2+5x−6|+K
b
 −2ln⁡|x|+12ln⁡|2x2+5x−6|+K
c
 −2x+ln⁡|2x2+5x−6|+K
d
 −2ln⁡|x|+2x2+5x−63+K
e
 −ln⁡|x|+2ln⁡|2x2+5x−6|+K
Submit

decision.explanation: The integrand equals −2/x+(4x+5)/(2x²+5x−6), since −2(2x²+5x−6)+x(4x+5)=12−5x. The second numerator is the derivative of its denominator, so integration gives −2ln|x|+ln|2x²+5x−6|+K, matching option a.

after.name: Question 15
after.worked_solution:
Notice that the quadratic factor in the denominator has a discriminant that is not a perfect square:

$$
D=(5)^{2}-4(2)(-6)=73
$$

We have that $\sqrt{73}$ is not a rational number, which implies that the quadratic factor doesn't factor over the rational numbers.

So, we proceed with the following partial fraction decomposition:

$$
\frac{12-5x}{x(2{x}^{2}+5x-6)}=\frac{A}{x}+\frac{Bx+C}{2{x}^{2}+5x-6}
$$

To determine the coefficients $A,B,$ and $C,$ we first multiply both sides of the above equation by $x(2{x}^{2}+5x-6),$ and we get

$$
12-5x=A(2{x}^{2}+5x-6)+(Bx+C)x
$$

Solving for the unknown constants using the usual methods, we get $A=-2,B=4$, and $C=5.$ Therefore,

$$
\frac{12-5x}{x(2{x}^{2}+5x-6)}=-\frac{2}{x}+\frac{4x+5}{2{x}^{2}+5x-6}.
$$

We now integrate this function term by term, adding the constant of integration at the very end.

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{12-5x}{x(2{x}^{2}+5x-6)}\,\text{d}x & =\int (-\frac{2}{x}+\frac{4x+5}{2{x}^{2}+5x-6})\,\text{d}x \\  & =-2\int \frac{1}{x}\,\text{d}x+\int \frac{4x+5}{2{x}^{2}+5x-6}\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

For the first integral, we have

$$
\int \frac{1}{x}\,\text{d}x=\operatorname{ln}⁡|x|.
$$

For the second integral, we use the substitution $u=2{x}^{2}+5x-6.$ Then $\text{d}u=(4x+5)\,\text{d}x,$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{4x+5}{2{x}^{2}+5x-6}\,\text{d}x & =\int (\frac{1}{u})\text{d}u \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡|u| \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡|2{x}^{2}+5x-6|\end{aligned}
$$

So, we get the following result:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{12-5x}{x(2{x}^{2}+5x-6)}\,\text{d}x & =-2\int \frac{1}{x}\,\text{d}x+\int \frac{4x+5}{2{x}^{2}+5x-6}\,\text{d}x \\  & =-2\operatorname{ln}⁡|x|+\operatorname{ln}⁡|2{x}^{2}+5x-6|+K.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 15
?

Evaluate the integral ∫12−5xx(2x2+5x−6)dx.

a
 −2ln⁡|x|+ln⁡|2x2+5x−6|+K
b
 −2ln⁡|x|+12ln⁡|2x2+5x−6|+K
c
 −2x+ln⁡|2x2+5x−6|+K
d
 −2ln⁡|x|+2x2+5x−63+K
e
 −ln⁡|x|+2ln⁡|2x2+5x−6|+K
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Notice that the quadratic factor in the denominator has a discriminant that is not a perfect square: D=(5)2−4(2)(−6)=73 We have that 73 is not a rational number, which implies that the quadratic factor doesn't factor over the rational numbers.

So, we proceed with the following partial fraction decomposition: 12−5xx(2x2+5x−6)=Ax+Bx+C2x2+5x−6

To determine the coefficients A,B, and C, we first multiply both sides of the above equation by x(2x2+5x−6), and we get

12−5x=A(2x2+5x−6)+(Bx+C)x

Solving for the unknown constants using the usual methods, we get A=−2,B=4, and C=5. Therefore, 12−5xx(2x2+5x−6)=−2x+4x+52x2+5x−6.

We now integrate this function term by term, adding the constant of integration at the very end.

∫12−5xx(2x2+5x−6)dx=∫(−2x+4x+52x2+5x−6)dx=−2∫1xdx+∫4x+52x2+5x−6dx.

For the first integral, we have ∫1xdx=ln⁡|x|.

For the second integral, we use the substitution u=2x2+5x−6. Then du=(4x+5)dx, and we get ∫4x+52x2+5x−6dx=∫(1u)du=ln⁡|u|=ln⁡|2x2+5x−6|

So, we get the following result: ∫12−5xx(2x2+5x−6)dx=−2∫1xdx+∫4x+52x2+5x−6dx=−2ln⁡|x|+ln⁡|2x2+5x−6|+K.

content.knowledge_point: Integrating a Rational Function With an Irreducible Trinomial Quadratic Factor
content.worked_solution:
Notice that the quadratic factor in the denominator has a discriminant that is not a perfect square:

$$
D=(5)^{2}-4(2)(-6)=73
$$

We have that $\sqrt{73}$ is not a rational number, which implies that the quadratic factor doesn't factor over the rational numbers.

So, we proceed with the following partial fraction decomposition:

$$
\frac{12-5x}{x(2{x}^{2}+5x-6)}=\frac{A}{x}+\frac{Bx+C}{2{x}^{2}+5x-6}
$$

To determine the coefficients $A,B,$ and $C,$ we first multiply both sides of the above equation by $x(2{x}^{2}+5x-6),$ and we get

$$
12-5x=A(2{x}^{2}+5x-6)+(Bx+C)x
$$

Solving for the unknown constants using the usual methods, we get $A=-2,B=4$, and $C=5.$ Therefore,

$$
\frac{12-5x}{x(2{x}^{2}+5x-6)}=-\frac{2}{x}+\frac{4x+5}{2{x}^{2}+5x-6}.
$$

We now integrate this function term by term, adding the constant of integration at the very end.

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{12-5x}{x(2{x}^{2}+5x-6)}\,\text{d}x & =\int (-\frac{2}{x}+\frac{4x+5}{2{x}^{2}+5x-6})\,\text{d}x \\  & =-2\int \frac{1}{x}\,\text{d}x+\int \frac{4x+5}{2{x}^{2}+5x-6}\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

For the first integral, we have

$$
\int \frac{1}{x}\,\text{d}x=\operatorname{ln}⁡|x|.
$$

For the second integral, we use the substitution $u=2{x}^{2}+5x-6.$ Then $\text{d}u=(4x+5)\,\text{d}x,$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{4x+5}{2{x}^{2}+5x-6}\,\text{d}x & =\int (\frac{1}{u})\text{d}u \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡|u| \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡|2{x}^{2}+5x-6|\end{aligned}
$$

So, we get the following result:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{12-5x}{x(2{x}^{2}+5x-6)}\,\text{d}x & =-2\int \frac{1}{x}\,\text{d}x+\int \frac{4x+5}{2{x}^{2}+5x-6}\,\text{d}x \\  & =-2\operatorname{ln}⁡|x|+\operatorname{ln}⁡|2{x}^{2}+5x-6|+K.\end{aligned}
$$
